EVENTS.h: Southern truckers ease roadblocks as cabinet approves diesel aid for hauliers
EVENTS.s: Truck drivers' protests that seriously affected fuel and food supplies in southern Italy were easing on 22 October, with hauliers saying roadblocks would be lifted in Sicily after talks with the government and drivers in Calabria suspending their protest. The deputy infrastructure minister said the blockades caused severe disruption in Campania to supermarkets, petrol stations and hospitals, and Naples doctors said fuel shortages were hampering ambulances. Meloni chaired a cabinet meeting to approve a decree compensating truckers and farmers for high diesel costs and offered police escorts for trucks carrying essential goods.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy's two crises moved in opposite directions on 22 October: trucker roadblocks over diesel prices that had emptied supermarket shelves and fuel pumps across the south, halted buffalo mozzarella production and disrupted ambulance and hospital access in Naples began to lift in Sicily and Calabria as the cabinet approved an aid decree for hauliers, farmers and fishers, while Meloni warned that remaining blockades and tyre-slashing of other drivers would be treated as intimidation.

EVENTS.h: 630 drones sent towards Moscow overnight, two wounded; Lipetsk apartment blocks hit
EVENTS.s: Moscow Mayor Sobyanin said 630 Ukrainian drones were sent towards the capital overnight on 21-22 October, most downed at long range, and two people were wounded near Moscow. In Lipetsk, some 400 km south of Moscow, a man was injured as drones hit apartment buildings and a medical facility, Governor Artamonov said. The attacks came hours after Witkoff's talks with Putin in St Petersburg.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: Reuters reported the 18 October assault on St Petersburg and the Leningrad region killed one and injured 15, set the St Petersburg oil terminal and an oil depot ablaze and hit Ozon and VK logistics and data centres as Russia claimed 1,015 drones downed in one night, while on 22 October 630 drones were sent towards Moscow, wounding two, and drones struck apartment buildings and a clinic in Lipetsk, hours after a drone killed a 19-year-old in Bryansk region on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Fighting between Oromia and Somali forces in Moyale drives hundreds into Kenya
EVENTS.s: Fighting broke out in the Ethiopian side of the border town of Moyale on 21 October and gunfire could still be heard a day later, residents told Reuters, with hundreds of Ethiopians, mainly women and children, crossing into Kenya's Marsabit county. Kenyan police said the arrivals were fleeing tensions between leaders of Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional states. The Kenya Red Cross said no camp was ready to host the displaced.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Tigray is easing but not settled: federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa, Axum and Zalambessa, Al Jazeera reported shops and banks reopening in Mekelle on 22 October, and Abiy's six-month caretaker administration named on 16 October is preparing an election, yet the TPLF rejects it, the Ethiopia-Eritrea confrontation remains frozen with troops facing each other at Zalambessa and Rubio warned on 17 October that troop surges on both sides of the border could turn into a broader conflict.

EVENTS.h: Air strike on ELN camp in Cauca kills nine, including regional commander
EVENTS.s: Nine members of the ELN were killed on Thursday in a military bombing of a camp in rural El Tambo, Cauca, President Abelardo de la Espriella said on social media. He said the dead included alias Marcos Pacífico, one of the group's main leaders in south-west Colombia. It is the fifth air strike ordered since he took office on 7 August.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Nariño, Catatumbo, Arauca; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali and overland travel on the Venezuelan border. President de la Espriella's government is escalating: a 22 October air strike on an ELN camp in El Tambo, Cauca killed nine guerrillas including the Southwestern War Front's military chief alias Marcos Pacífico (DW, 23 Oct), the fifth bombing of his term, three days after he ordered a 'total offensive' against the ELN and FARC dissidents from Arauca and demanded the ELN free five hostages including two CTI investigators (Presidencia, 19 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Ukrainian national arrested in Brandenburg on suspicion of spying for Russia
EVENTS.s: Federal prosecutors said a Ukrainian national identified as Vadym Y. was arrested in Brandenburg on 22 October on suspicion of spying for a Russian intelligence service via an intermediary since at least July 2025. He is accused of gathering information on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition and explosives and on personnel and installations securing NATO's eastern flank, partly by approaching people in the European defence industry. He was due before a Federal Court of Justice judge on 23 October.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment hardened further this week: federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian national in Brandenburg on 22 October for gathering military intelligence for Russia, including on NATO eastern-flank sites and defence-industry production, one day after the Bundeswehr rated the Russian sabotage threat to its own forces as significant for the first time, citing the explosive-laden drone found near Wunstorf air base.

EVENTS.h: Thousands rally peacefully in Paris after court overturns police protest ban
EVENTS.s: Thousands of protesters, many of them students, gathered peacefully in south-eastern Paris on 22 October under heavy police presence after an administrative court overturned a prefecture ban, while demonstrations planned in Lyon, Lille and Grenoble were banned. Organisers signed a police document keeping the protest stationary because of the risk of violence. After a security meeting at the Elysée, Macron said protests requested by groups with no legitimate authority will be banned in the coming days and marches in Lyon, Marseille and Montpellier for Saturday will also be banned.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning. France remains the epicentre of the European unrest wave: the 17 October riots torched Limoges town hall, damaged or looted more than 3,000 shops and put some 2,500 people in custody, and the government has responded with targeted night curfews in Paris, Lyon, Lille, Nice, Bordeaux and Marseille, protest bans in Paris, Lyon, Lille and Grenoble and troops alongside police for the Saturday 24 October protest day, which yellow-vest activists and the CGT union have joined.

EVENTS.h: Police fire tear gas at Tunis suburb protesters after custody death; Sfax clashes
EVENTS.s: Tunisian police fired tear gas on Thursday to disperse protesters in Ettadhamen after the death of a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing, whose family said he died from police violence after arrest; local media said he died after swallowing drugs. Protesters blocked roads, burned tyres and threw stones at police, who moved to secure a National Guard station. Earlier the same day police clashed with protesters in Jebeniana after the death of a man his relatives say died during a security chase, with similar clashes in Agareb and a student protest in Sfax.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid central Tunis, Ettadhamen and Sfax-area flashpoints on protest days. Tunisia's risk profile is rising: on 22 October police fired tear gas at protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of Tunis, after the death of a man in custody, with parallel clashes in Jebeniana and Agareb in Sfax governorate and student protests in Sfax city (Reuters), five days after the UGTT-led march of 17 October, the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years.

EVENTS.h: Egypt urges Yemen talks as parliament weighs defensive military support for Saudi Arabia
EVENTS.s: Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said Egypt wants to 'explore every opportunity' for a political solution to the Yemen conflict, ahead of the 26 October parliamentary vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Houthis. Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter from President Sisi to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman stating that any support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders. The Houthi-run parliament's speaker warned on 17 October that Egyptian involvement would pose 'a grave threat to its own national security and internal stability'.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · Red Sea/Suez watch; North Sinai and Sudan border restricted. No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was wire-confirmed in Egypt for 9-23 October, but the external-security profile is rising.

EVENTS.h: Pipeline valve shut at Zawiya station cuts output at Hamada and Tahara oilfields
EVENTS.s: The head of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Thursday that a valve on the AGOCO pipeline carrying crude from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port had been shut, reducing production at both fields. NOC said individuals entered the crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and closed the valve without coordination, warning that a continued shutdown 'will lead to the loss of volumes of crude oil production', and urged the authorities 'to intervene immediately to reopen the valve and secure the site'. Hamada produces about 50,000 bpd under stable conditions; an armed group shut valve 7 on the Sharara-Zawiya pipeline in September.
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical and the trend is rising: on 22 October individuals entered the AGOCO crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and shut the valve on the Hamada-Tahara pipeline, cutting output at both fields (Reuters), the second forced pipeline closure in western Libya in five weeks; on 21 October armed men stormed the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose a disputed deputy head, drawing UNSMIL's strongest condemnation and a warning of targeted sanctions; and on 18 October an 82mm mortar blast killed at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency personnel during training in Zawiya (Reuters).

EVENTS.h: Stray bullets hit Kenyan side of Moyale as hundreds flee fighting in Ethiopia
EVENTS.s: Kenyan police said hundreds of Ethiopians crossed into Kenya through several entry points in Moyale from 21 October, fleeing tensions between leaders of Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional states, with gunfire heard on the Ethiopian side from about 05:50 on 22 October. A 31-year-old woman was shot in the neck and treated at a private hospital, a police officer was struck on the head by a bullet that hit a tent support at the Moyale police station ground, and a bullet shattered a window at the La-Tahsan Hotel.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · health screening. Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating normally but the risk picture carries a health overlay: the imported Bundibugyo Ebola case has produced a nine-case cluster of relatives and healthcare workers as of 20 October, all detected in quarantine with 134 of 135 contacts traced and no transmission outside the group, and the US moved Kenya to Level 3 on 19 October while keeping Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu and Tana River at Do Not Travel over kidnapping and terrorism.

EVENTS.h: Lula files to disqualify Bolsonaro a day after rival's petition, three days before runoff
EVENTS.s: President Lula's campaign asked the Superior Electoral Court on Wednesday to disqualify Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for abuse of economic power and improper use of social networks, citing Meta's handling of campaign content. Bolsonaro's lawyers had filed on Tuesday to annul Lula's candidacy over mass government messaging on WhatsApp. Polls show a technical tie ahead of the 25 October vote.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct; avoid favela-adjacent routes, Avenida Brasil at night and election-day crowds; expect result-related gatherings in Brasília, São Paulo and Rio on Sunday night. Brazil votes on Sunday 25 October in a presidential runoff that Quaest (Reuters, 21 Oct) puts at 45-44 for Flávio Bolsonaro over Lula, within the margin of error, and on 20-21 October each camp filed a petition at the Superior Electoral Court to disqualify the other (AFP, 22 Oct), so a narrow result is likely to be contested in court and on the street.

EVENTS.adm: Caracas, Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal, Maracaibo
EVENTS.h: Thousands join first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years
EVENTS.s: Thousands of Venezuelans marched on Thursday in Caracas and other cities in the first nationwide opposition protest since early 2025, demanding free elections by July 2027 and the release of political prisoners. The ruling Socialist Party called a march from Plaza Venezuela, the opposition's planned gathering point, two hours earlier, and Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello attended it while opposition supporters moved to a nearby location. Security forces kept a notably thin presence.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · Caracas workable with advance; stand off from all demonstrations and party marches in central Caracas (Plaza Venezuela, Miraflores approaches), low profile, no overland border travel. The first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years passed on 22 October without wire-reported violence: thousands marched in Caracas, Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal and Maracaibo for a 2027 election date, Machado's return and the release of more than 320 political prisoners, with a thin security-force presence even as the ruling party held a rival march from the same square (Reuters, 22 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Shops and banks reopen in Mekelle as border communities fear wider war
EVENTS.s: Al Jazeera reported on 22 October that shops were reopening and banks resuming services in Mekelle under federal control, though residents remained anxious. Near the Eritrean border, military movements and conflicting accounts of troop deployments have heightened fears that the fighting could spread beyond Tigray; Ethiopia's foreign minister accused Eritrea on 8 October of sending troops up to 60 km into Tigray.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Tigray is easing but not settled: federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa, Axum and Zalambessa, Al Jazeera reported shops and banks reopening in Mekelle on 22 October, and Abiy's six-month caretaker administration named on 16 October is preparing an election, yet the TPLF rejects it, the Ethiopia-Eritrea confrontation remains frozen with troops facing each other at Zalambessa and Rubio warned on 17 October that troop surges on both sides of the border could turn into a broader conflict.

EVENTS.h: China and Djibouti call for Red Sea freedom of navigation as Yemen fighting escalates
EVENTS.s: China and Djibouti said in a joint statement after their foreign ministers met in Beijing that all countries should enjoy freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, expressing concern about the deteriorating security situation. The statement said major powers outside the region should respect the sovereignty of littoral states and avoid resorting to force. It came as the US State Department ordered some diplomats and family members to leave Saudi Arabia after an escalation of fighting in Yemen.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · transit hub. No violent security incident was recorded inside Djibouti in the past 14 days; the major event remains the 8-9 October migrant shipwreck off Obock (139 dead and 84 missing per IOM), while UNHCR counted 3,836 refugees arrived from Yemen in Obock region by 17 October with an acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in the Markazi camp.

EVENTS.h: Bundeswehr rates Russian sabotage threat 'significant' after explosive drone near air base
EVENTS.s: Germany's armed forces classified the threat of Russian sabotage against their troops and facilities as significant for the first time, the second-highest level on their internal scale, a defence ministry spokesperson confirmed on 21 October. The assessment was triggered by a crashed drone carrying high explosives found near Wunstorf air base in mid-September and cites drone overflights of the Arrow 3 site and a hidden camera at Minden rail station. Intelligence services expect further actions in the near future.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment hardened further this week: federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian national in Brandenburg on 22 October for gathering military intelligence for Russia, including on NATO eastern-flank sites and defence-industry production, one day after the Bundeswehr rated the Russian sabotage threat to its own forces as significant for the first time, citing the explosive-laden drone found near Wunstorf air base.

EVENTS.h: Missile fired at Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil
EVENTS.s: A missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October, security sources told Reuters. No casualties were reported. It followed Iranian drone strikes on exile camps in Erbil province on 8, 12 and 17 October.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: a missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October (Reuters), the latest in a series of Iranian strikes on exile camps on 8, 12 and 17 October, and on 20 October Tehran's ambassador said Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups, a step Iraqi security officials had told AFP they refused.

EVENTS.h: Military court sentences opposition leader Olfa Hamdi to four years in prison
EVENTS.s: A military court sentenced Third Republic Party leader Olfa Hamdi, who holds US citizenship, to four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the military to disobey orders, her lawyer Akram Moussa told Reuters. The sentence comprises two separate two-year terms and fines totalling 80,000 dinars ($26,000); Hamdi was already sentenced to two years in March in a separate case. A US State Department spokesman told AFP Washington was 'closely tracking the situation'.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid central Tunis, Ettadhamen and Sfax-area flashpoints on protest days. Tunisia's risk profile is rising: on 22 October police fired tear gas at protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of Tunis, after the death of a man in custody, with parallel clashes in Jebeniana and Agareb in Sfax governorate and student protests in Sfax city (Reuters), five days after the UGTT-led march of 17 October, the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years.

EVENTS.h: Armed men storm National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose disputed deputy head
EVENTS.s: UNSMIL condemned 'in the strongest possible terms' the use of force and intimidation at the headquarters of the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli in an attempt to install a disputed deputy head of the institution. The mission called for an immediate end to armed interference and the withdrawal of armed personnel from the premises, and warned that those responsible for attacks on state institutions 'risk being subjected to targeted sanctions' under Security Council resolutions. The Audit Bureau said it suspended work after the armed raid.
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical and the trend is rising: on 22 October individuals entered the AGOCO crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and shut the valve on the Hamada-Tahara pipeline, cutting output at both fields (Reuters), the second forced pipeline closure in western Libya in five weeks; on 21 October armed men stormed the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose a disputed deputy head, drawing UNSMIL's strongest condemnation and a warning of targeted sanctions; and on 18 October an 82mm mortar blast killed at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency personnel during training in Zawiya (Reuters).

EVENTS.h: Austrian and Swiss women freed after 18 months' captivity in Niger reach Benghazi
EVENTS.s: Austrian aid worker Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss community worker Claudia Abbt, 69, kidnapped separately in Agadez in January and April 2025, were freed and handed to authorities in Benghazi, Libya, in an operation overseen by Saddam Haftar. Both governments confirmed the releases on 22 October; no group has claimed the abductions, though reports have linked them to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of the release were not disclosed.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · essential travel only with state-level clearance. The deadliest incident of the window struck the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen in three vehicles ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP), on the only corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic between Agadez and the uranium belt, and the military escort aboard did not prevent it.

EVENTS.h: IOM warns 874,000 could be displaced by El Niño floods by December
EVENTS.s: IOM said on 21 October that projections with the Danish Refugee Council estimate 874,319 people could be displaced in Somalia between October and December, 92 per cent of them by flooding, as the Deyr rains arrive under strengthening El Niño conditions. The Juba River at Dollow is approaching flood level, the Shabelle is near the top of its banks at Jowhar, and heavy rain in Baidoa has already damaged homes; Beledweyne (229,000) and Galkayo (82,000) face the greatest displacement risk. IOM has secured only 14.4 per cent of the USD 16.62 million it needs for flood preparedness.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. As of 23 October, AFP-confirmed reporting shows Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces holding Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle (30 km from Baidoa), leaving Baidoa as the only major Bay town under the federally backed South West administration, which has vowed to retake the districts while Ethiopian AUSSOM troops stayed inside their bases; a fight for Baidoa remains the base case and the Mogadishu–Baidoa road through Buurhakaba is cut.

EVENTS.h: Slovakia to resume intergovernmental talks with Russia in Moscow on 26 October
EVENTS.s: The Slovak Foreign Ministry said the Russian-Slovak intergovernmental commission for economic, scientific and technical cooperation will meet in Moscow on 26 October, the first session since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The agenda centres on energy, including gas and continued oil supplies and nuclear power, plus farming, environment, sport and culture. Slovakia is meant to end Russian gas purchases by late 2027 under EU plans.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, violent protest or transport disruption was confirmed in Slovakia between 9 and 23 October.

EVENTS.h: Zelensky visits Storting, meets parliamentary leaders after Oslo talks
EVENTS.s: President Zelensky visited the Storting on 21 October for meetings with its President Masud Gharahkhani, the parliamentary leaders and the chair of the Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee. The visit followed the previous day's Oslo talks hosted by Støre and Stubb with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · heightened hybrid vigilance. Norway remains a low-risk operating environment; the only in-window events affecting movement were the heavily policed 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Støre and Stubb and Zelensky's 21 October visit to the Storting, both of which passed without incident.

EVENTS.h: Putin frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard as Witkoff opens St Petersburg talks
EVENTS.s: Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired US schoolteacher held since 2022 on mercenary charges, on 21 October and took him to St Petersburg's Pulkovo airport to fly home. Putin announced the release at a meeting with US envoy Steve Witkoff, and the Kremlin said Putin agreed to resume US-mediated trilateral talks with Kyiv as soon as next month.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: Reuters reported the 18 October assault on St Petersburg and the Leningrad region killed one and injured 15, set the St Petersburg oil terminal and an oil depot ablaze and hit Ozon and VK logistics and data centres as Russia claimed 1,015 drones downed in one night, while on 22 October 630 drones were sent towards Moscow, wounding two, and drones struck apartment buildings and a clinic in Lipetsk, hours after a drone killed a 19-year-old in Bryansk region on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Istanbul prosecutors order detention of 31 suspects in investment-fund probe
EVENTS.s: The Istanbul chief prosecutor's office on 21 October ordered the detention of 31 suspects in an investigation into share transactions in four listed companies, with 26 in custody by the time of reporting. The probe follows complaints from the Capital Markets Board and is part of a wider investigation into Turkey's investment-fund sector, in which dozens of funds were ordered liquidated last month.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye in the 9-23 October window; the operational picture is dominated by the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight dead per AFP on 19 October) and by the political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October (Reuters), continuing detentions of opposition-run municipal officials, and Reuters-reported detention orders for 31 suspects in the investment-fund probe on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Eritrea restates defensive posture, denies invasion claims and blames Addis for instability
EVENTS.s: Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement on 21 October titled 'Eritrea's Principled Position Regarding the Ongoing Situation with Ethiopia', describing the inviolability of its sovereign boundary as a principle on which every African border depends. The statement accused Ethiopia's ruling Prosperity Party of coveting Eritrea's coast as 'strategically necessary' and set out a framework for regional peace based on non-interference and adherence to international law.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea remains a party to the Tigray confrontation in all but name: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, Asmara asked the Council for Chapter VII deterrent measures against Ethiopia on 10 October, and Ethiopian troops reached Zalambessa on the border on 13 October.

EVENTS.h: France to deploy troops for 24 October protests, admits failures over riots
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu told parliament on 20 October that the security deployment for Saturday 24 October will be massive and that troops will reinforce police, acknowledging intelligence failures and static deployments during the 17 October riots in Paris, Marseille and Lyon. Targeted curfews, some aimed at under-18s, brought a night of relative calm and were extended; the student union UNEF called further protests for Saturday. Lawmakers agreed to launch a parliamentary inquiry into the unrest.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning. France remains the epicentre of the European unrest wave: the 17 October riots torched Limoges town hall, damaged or looted more than 3,000 shops and put some 2,500 people in custody, and the government has responded with targeted night curfews in Paris, Lyon, Lille, Nice, Bordeaux and Marseille, protest bans in Paris, Lyon, Lille and Grenoble and troops alongside police for the Saturday 24 October protest day, which yellow-vest activists and the CGT union have joined.

EVENTS.h: Nigeria confirms imported Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja; 44 contacts traced
EVENTS.s: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on 20 October: a Ugandan woman who arrived in Abuja via Addis Ababa on 5 October, fell ill two days later and was tested only on 19 October after treatment at a private hospital. Authorities identified 44 contacts, most of them healthcare workers, including her Swiss husband. The outbreak strain is Bundibugyo, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment; the health minister said on 22 October there was no evidence of community spread.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja Ebola watch. The north-east is in its most dangerous phase in years: Boko Haram overran the army base at Guzamala on the night of 13 October, killing at least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard (Reuters, 15 Oct), and a mine-and-ambush attack on a patrol between Gamboru Ngala and the Cameroon border on 17 October killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF members (Reuters, 19 Oct); in the north-west, bandits killed at least 20 in a military-escorted traders' convoy in Bukkuyum, Zamfara, on 10 October (Reuters, 12 Oct), so armed escort cannot be treated as sufficient mitigation on rural roads.

EVENTS.h: Gunmen ambush two escorted passenger buses near Agadez, killing at least 11
EVENTS.s: Gunmen aboard three vehicles attacked two buses that had left the mining town of Arlit on the morning of 20 October, just outside Agadez, killing at least 11 passengers and wounding several more, local broadcaster Tegades TV reported and an Agadez resident confirmed to AFP. Soldiers escorting the convoy exchanged fire with the attackers. Niger's arid north is a trafficking corridor and has seen violence linked to wildcat gold mining.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · essential travel only with state-level clearance. The deadliest incident of the window struck the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen in three vehicles ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP), on the only corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic between Agadez and the uranium belt, and the military escort aboard did not prevent it.

EVENTS.h: Two re-arrested under National Security Act for assisting Iranian intelligence
EVENTS.s: Counter Terrorism Policing re-arrested a 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national on 20 October on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service, as part of the investigation into activity near RAF Fairford on 27 September. Seven men had earlier been arrested and bailed. The head of counter-terrorism policing said Iranian state involvement is considered highly likely.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity. The UK picture through 23 October is dominated by state threats rather than street disorder: the RAF Fairford investigation moved on 20 October to National Security Act re-arrests for assisting Iranian intelligence, MI5 said on 13 October that Iran and Russia are both expanding hybrid campaigns and that Iran-linked operations produced more than 50 arrests in a year, and the Home Secretary set out new sanctions and powers on 12 October.

EVENTS.h: Cabinet sends 500 troops to Milan and creates violent-protest offence
EVENTS.s: The Italian cabinet approved a decree on 20 October deploying an additional 500 soldiers to Milan through the end of the year, creating a new offence of violent participation in a demonstration punishable by up to five years in prison and a fine of up to 20,000 euros, and making parents liable for damage caused by minors. Police said about 2,000 youths took part in the Milan riots on 17 October and more than 100 officers were injured over two days. Parliament must convert the decree within 60 days.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy's two crises moved in opposite directions on 22 October: trucker roadblocks over diesel prices that had emptied supermarket shelves and fuel pumps across the south, halted buffalo mozzarella production and disrupted ambulance and hospital access in Naples began to lift in Sicily and Calabria as the cabinet approved an aid decree for hauliers, farmers and fishers, while Meloni warned that remaining blockades and tyre-slashing of other drivers would be treated as intimidation.

EVENTS.h: Iran says Iraq agreed to expel or hand over Iranian Kurdish opposition groups
EVENTS.s: Iran's ambassador to Iraq said on 20 October that Baghdad had agreed at a joint security commission to expel members of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups from Iraqi Kurdistan or hand them to Iran. Senior Iraqi security officials had earlier told AFP that Baghdad refused to expel the exiles, citing fears for their lives.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: a missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October (Reuters), the latest in a series of Iranian strikes on exile camps on 8, 12 and 17 October, and on 20 October Tehran's ambassador said Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups, a step Iraqi security officials had told AFP they refused.

EVENTS.h: UN chief condemns Abyei drone strikes, calls on Khartoum and Juba to prevent repeat
EVENTS.s: The UN Secretary-General condemned the 19 October drone attacks near Amiet market and Todach that killed dozens of civilians including women and children, saying the toll was expected to rise as UNISFA verified casualties with many missing. He said there would need to be accountability and called on Sudan and South Sudan to uphold Abyei's demilitarised status. UNISFA deployed medical, firefighting and quick-reaction units and intensified day and night patrols.
EVENTS.impl: No-go outside Juba · essential travel only. South Sudan is absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October strike on Amiet market in Abyei, which hit a fuel depot and which a Sudanese military officer told AP targeted RSF-bound fuel tankers, killed at least 153 by the Abyei administration's count given to Reuters and AP and displaced about 8,000; UNISFA said on 21 October that many remain missing and the toll is expected to rise.

EVENTS.h: Kenya confirms ninth Ebola case; all linked to index patient, no community spread
EVENTS.s: Kenya's health ministry confirmed a ninth Bundibugyo Ebola case on 20 October, a 24-year-old close family member of the first patient who was already in quarantine. Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said all nine cases belong to one cluster with no evidence of transmission outside the group, and that 134 of 135 contacts had been traced and quarantined. The first patient travelled from DRC via Uganda and died at Nairobi Hospital on 5 October.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · health screening. Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating normally but the risk picture carries a health overlay: the imported Bundibugyo Ebola case has produced a nine-case cluster of relatives and healthcare workers as of 20 October, all detected in quarantine with 134 of 135 contacts traced and no transmission outside the group, and the US moved Kenya to Level 3 on 19 October while keeping Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu and Tana River at Do Not Travel over kidnapping and terrorism.

EVENTS.h: Zelensky meets Witkoff, Støre and Stubb in Oslo under heavy security
EVENTS.s: Ukrainian President Zelensky held talks in Oslo on 20 October with US envoy Steve Witkoff, hosted by Prime Minister Støre and Finnish President Stubb, with Jared Kushner joining by video. The meeting sought to repair US-Ukraine relations and passed without incident.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · heightened hybrid vigilance. Norway remains a low-risk operating environment; the only in-window events affecting movement were the heavily policed 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Støre and Stubb and Zelensky's 21 October visit to the Storting, both of which passed without incident.

EVENTS.h: Sudanese drone strike on Abyei's Amiet market kills at least 153
EVENTS.s: Drones struck Amiet market north of Abyei town at about 11:00 on 19 October, hitting a fuel depot and starting fires that were still burning a day later. Abyei's caretaker information minister Yohana Akol Ngor told Reuters the toll had risen from 73 to 153 and could climb further; South Sudan's foreign ministry blamed Sudan's army and summoned its ambassador. MSF treated more than 20 wounded, including burns and critical cases, at Ameth Bek hospital.
EVENTS.impl: No-go outside Juba · essential travel only. South Sudan is absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October strike on Amiet market in Abyei, which hit a fuel depot and which a Sudanese military officer told AP targeted RSF-bound fuel tankers, killed at least 153 by the Abyei administration's count given to Reuters and AP and displaced about 8,000; UNISFA said on 21 October that many remain missing and the toll is expected to rise.

EVENTS.h: Storm Adam floods eastern Spain: four dead, more than 2,000 evacuated
EVENTS.s: Torrential rain from Storm Adam killed four people, two in Oliva, one at a beach in Sagunto and one swept into a stream in Catalonia, and triggered helicopter rescues of residents from rooftops in southern Valencia and northern Alicante. Pego recorded 632 mm of rain in 36 hours; about 800,000 residents were under shelter-in-place orders on the morning of 19 October, falling to 87,000 in eight municipalities by late afternoon. More than 2,000 people were evacuated, mainly in Oliva, and more than 400 rescues were carried out in the Valencia region.
EVENTS.src: Al Jazeera with AFP and Reuters, 20 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · weather recovery and protest watch. Spain's immediate risk remains environmental: Storm Adam killed four people in the Valencia region and Catalonia on 17-19 October, with 632 mm of rain in 36 hours at Pego, more than 2,000 evacuated and up to 800,000 people briefly under shelter-in-place orders; red alerts have been lifted but clean-up in Oliva, Pego, Els Poblets and the Marina Alta continues to disrupt secondary roads and commuter rail.

EVENTS.h: HRW: Malian army and Africa Corps drone strikes killed scores of civilians
EVENTS.s: Human Rights Watch said on 19 October that Malian forces and Russia's Africa Corps used apparent indiscriminate drone strikes in their offensive since April, and that the number of strikes and civilian deaths between April and August roughly doubled compared with a year earlier. Documented cases include an 19 August strike on a cattle market in Bandiagara that killed six men and a 29 July strike on a health centre in Kidal region. The report also documented the execution of 19 captured soldiers by JNIM and FLA fighters in Gao region in July.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Mali is in open, multi-front war: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a fuel blockade since late April, while Islamic State Sahel Province's killing of at least 48 civilians (provisional local tolls up to 70+) across at least five localities in Menaka on 18-19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, shows the IS affiliate escalating in the east even as it fights JNIM across the Burkina border; the army said on 19 October it had struck a major ISSP base 65 km south-west of Menaka (AP).

EVENTS.h: RSF drones hit Khartoum airport district killing four; army strike on Nyala kills 17
EVENTS.s: A drone strike on a house in the Nasser Extension neighbourhood east of Khartoum airport on the morning of 19 October killed four people including three children aged two to six, a medical source said; the army said air defences intercepted RSF drones targeting the airport and the Atbara and Setit dams in Gadaref state. Hours earlier an army drone strike on central Nyala, the RSF-held capital of South Darfur, killed 17 people including seven RSF officers and wounded 23, medical and RSF sources said.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. The war is in a drone-dominated phase in which both sides strike far behind the front lines: AFP counted at least 80 dead when army drones hit a transport hub beside Al-Dibab market in West Kordofan on 18 October, AP and AFP reported a strike on central Nyala on 19 October that killed 17 and an RSF drone attack the same morning on a house east of Khartoum airport that killed four, and the army's 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market across the South Sudan border killed at least 153 by the Abyei administration's count.

EVENTS.h: Polish-Ukrainian reservist on officer course detained on spying suspicion
EVENTS.s: Polish military police detained a Polish-Ukrainian dual national suspected of spying who was attending an officer training course for reservists in Łódź, authorities said on 19 October. The case follows a series of Russian-attributed sabotage and espionage incidents in Poland this autumn.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: three school stabbings in four days that killed a custodian and triggered checks of nearly 50,000 schools, German arrests on 12 October of two Turkish nationals suspected of the Russian-directed Starlink station arson near Warsaw, and the 19 October detention in Łódź of a Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course on spying suspicion.

EVENTS.h: Parliament delays vote on military support for Saudi Arabia to 26 October
EVENTS.s: Egypt's parliament delayed until 26 October a vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, after two emergency sessions on 18 and 19 October failed to reach a vote. The National Defence Council had pledged 'all necessary and possible' support to the kingdom on 18 October. Authorisation requires a two-thirds majority of the 596-member chamber, and the Egyptian Social Democratic Party instructed its lawmakers to abstain citing a lack of detail on the mission's objectives, duration and cost.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · Red Sea/Suez watch; North Sinai and Sudan border restricted. No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was wire-confirmed in Egypt for 9-23 October, but the external-security profile is rising.

EVENTS.h: Malian army says it struck major ISSP base south-west of Menaka
EVENTS.s: The Malian army announced on Monday 19 October that it had located and struck a major base housing several terrorist elements as well as military equipment and logistical supplies 65 km south-west of Menaka town. The statement followed the weekend ISSP attacks on civilians in the region. No casualty figures were given.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Mali is in open, multi-front war: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a fuel blockade since late April, while Islamic State Sahel Province's killing of at least 48 civilians (provisional local tolls up to 70+) across at least five localities in Menaka on 18-19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, shows the IS affiliate escalating in the east even as it fights JNIM across the Burkina border; the army said on 19 October it had struck a major ISSP base 65 km south-west of Menaka (AP).

EVENTS.h: Yemeni refugee arrivals in Obock reach 3,836 as diarrhoea outbreak hits camp
EVENTS.s: UNICEF's 19 October flash update said 3,836 refugees had arrived in Djibouti from Yemen since September according to UNHCR, with children making up 52 percent and 23 new arrivals recorded between 10 and 16 October. An acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in Markazi refugee village had produced 56 cases and three deaths by 17 October, with the first host-community case reported on 14 October. UNICEF's six-month appeal was 12 percent funded.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · transit hub. No violent security incident was recorded inside Djibouti in the past 14 days; the major event remains the 8-9 October migrant shipwreck off Obock (139 dead and 84 missing per IOM), while UNHCR counted 3,836 refugees arrived from Yemen in Obock region by 17 October with an acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in the Markazi camp.

EVENTS.h: US raises Kenya travel advisory to Level 3 over Ebola, crime, terrorism
EVENTS.s: The US State Department raised its Kenya travel advisory from Level 2 to Level 3 'Reconsider Travel' on 19 October, citing health risks alongside crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest and traffic safety. The advisory keeps Do Not Travel guidance for Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu and Tana River counties and coastal areas north of Malindi over kidnapping and terrorism, and notes that medical facilities often lack sufficient medicine and equipment.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · health screening. Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating normally but the risk picture carries a health overlay: the imported Bundibugyo Ebola case has produced a nine-case cluster of relatives and healthcare workers as of 20 October, all detected in quarantine with 134 of 135 contacts traced and no transmission outside the group, and the US moved Kenya to Level 3 on 19 October while keeping Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu and Tana River at Do Not Travel over kidnapping and terrorism.

EVENTS.h: Queimados municipal secretary shot dead by Military Police on Avenida Brasil
EVENTS.s: Jefferson Dias da Silva, 51, Queimados' economic development secretary and a former councillor, was killed on Monday night when officers of the 22nd Military Police Battalion fired on his car during an attempted stop on Avenida Brasil near Bonsucesso. The Military Police opened an internal procedure and the acting state governor ordered the officers involved removed from duty; the Civil Police homicide division is analysing body-camera footage. Two lanes of the artery were closed for the forensic work.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct; avoid favela-adjacent routes, Avenida Brasil at night and election-day crowds; expect result-related gatherings in Brasília, São Paulo and Rio on Sunday night. Brazil votes on Sunday 25 October in a presidential runoff that Quaest (Reuters, 21 Oct) puts at 45-44 for Flávio Bolsonaro over Lula, within the margin of error, and on 20-21 October each camp filed a petition at the Superior Electoral Court to disqualify the other (AFP, 22 Oct), so a narrow result is likely to be contested in court and on the street.

EVENTS.h: President orders 'total offensive' against ELN and FARC dissidents from Arauca
EVENTS.s: After a security council at the army's 18th Brigade in Arauca, President de la Espriella said he had ordered a total offensive against the ELN's Domingo Laín front and the FARC-dissident Estructura 10, targeting leaders, logistics and financiers, with reinforced troops, intelligence and land and river control of the Venezuelan border. He ordered jailed guerrilla leaders moved out of Arauca to maximum-security prisons and demanded the ELN release five hostages, including two CTI investigators. The government said homicides in the department fell 56.3% and attacks on security forces 71% between 7 August and 15 October.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Nariño, Catatumbo, Arauca; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali and overland travel on the Venezuelan border. President de la Espriella's government is escalating: a 22 October air strike on an ELN camp in El Tambo, Cauca killed nine guerrillas including the Southwestern War Front's military chief alias Marcos Pacífico (DW, 23 Oct), the fifth bombing of his term, three days after he ordered a 'total offensive' against the ELN and FARC dissidents from Arauca and demanded the ELN free five hostages including two CTI investigators (Presidencia, 19 Oct).

EVENTS.h: New El Mansouri government presents programme targeting 5% growth in 2027-2031
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri presented her government's five-year programme to parliament on Monday, targeting average annual growth of 5% between 2027 and 2031. Her four-party coalition, sworn in before King Mohammed VI on 16 October, holds 207 of the 395 seats in the House of Representatives. The programme prioritises anti-corruption measures, social welfare and youth employment.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · open for business. Morocco recorded no kinetic security incident between 9 and 23 October that a wire service confirmed; the environment remains political.

EVENTS.h: Spain's rush to clear Ceuta migrant backlog raises rights concerns
EVENTS.s: Reuters reported that eight charities including Oxfam and Amnesty International filed a complaint with Spain's ombudsman alleging 'grave rights violations' in the Ceuta enclave as Madrid moves to clear the asylum backlog left by the July mass crossing from Morocco. The dispute follows King Mohammed VI's 9 October statement that the migration cooperation model with Spain had reached its limit and the Spanish royals' 13 October visit to Ceuta.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · open for business. Morocco recorded no kinetic security incident between 9 and 23 October that a wire service confirmed; the environment remains political.

EVENTS.h: Largest-ever drone attack on St Petersburg kills one, injures 15, sets oil terminal ablaze
EVENTS.s: One person was killed and 15 injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on oil facilities, logistics and data centres in St Petersburg and the Leningrad region on 18 October, local authorities said. Governor Beglov said fires broke out at the St Petersburg oil terminal, an oil depot and industrial warehouses; Ozon's logistics hub burned and VK's data centre was hit. Russia's Defence Ministry said it downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: Reuters reported the 18 October assault on St Petersburg and the Leningrad region killed one and injured 15, set the St Petersburg oil terminal and an oil depot ablaze and hit Ozon and VK logistics and data centres as Russia claimed 1,015 drones downed in one night, while on 22 October 630 drones were sent towards Moscow, wounding two, and drones struck apartment buildings and a clinic in Lipetsk, hours after a drone killed a 19-year-old in Bryansk region on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: ISSP kills at least 48 civilians in Menaka in reprisal over informant killings
EVENTS.s: Islamic State Sahel Province fighters attacked at least five localities in the Menaka region from Sunday night 18 October into Monday morning, killing at least 48 people, with provisional tolls from four Reuters sources ranging from 48 to more than 70. The attackers torched homes and stole livestock, sending hundreds fleeing to Menaka town; the sources said the raids followed abuses the previous week by the pro-government MSA militia and Africa Corps against civilians suspected of informing for Islamic State. ISSP has not claimed responsibility.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Mali is in open, multi-front war: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a fuel blockade since late April, while Islamic State Sahel Province's killing of at least 48 civilians (provisional local tolls up to 70+) across at least five localities in Menaka on 18-19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, shows the IS affiliate escalating in the east even as it fights JNIM across the Burkina border; the army said on 19 October it had struck a major ISSP base 65 km south-west of Menaka (AP).

EVENTS.h: Drone strike on West Kordofan transport hub kills at least 80 after market day
EVENTS.s: A drone struck twice, ten minutes apart, at a transport hub where villagers were gathering rides home from Al-Dibab market on the evening of 18 October. A medical source told AFP 80 people were killed, including 30 of 47 wounded who died after transfer to Al-Mujlad; the RSF-declared Tasis administration and the Emergency Lawyers group accused the army, which did not comment. The UN Secretary-General's spokesman condemned the strike on 20 October.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. The war is in a drone-dominated phase in which both sides strike far behind the front lines: AFP counted at least 80 dead when army drones hit a transport hub beside Al-Dibab market in West Kordofan on 18 October, AP and AFP reported a strike on central Nyala on 19 October that killed 17 and an RSF drone attack the same morning on a house east of Khartoum airport that killed four, and the army's 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market across the South Sudan border killed at least 153 by the Abyei administration's count.

EVENTS.h: Second day of Milan rioting: stones, looting, 271 young people detained
EVENTS.s: Milan police clashed on 18 October with protesters throwing stones and looting shops near Piazza Duomo, firing tear gas and using water cannon after several hundred hooded protesters broke shop windows and set bins on fire. Authorities said 271 young people were detained in Milan on Sunday. A total of 28 protesters were arrested after similar clashes on 17 October in Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy's two crises moved in opposite directions on 22 October: trucker roadblocks over diesel prices that had emptied supermarket shelves and fuel pumps across the south, halted buffalo mozzarella production and disrupted ambulance and hospital access in Naples began to lift in Sicily and Calabria as the cabinet approved an aid decree for hauliers, farmers and fishers, while Meloni warned that remaining blockades and tyre-slashing of other drivers would be treated as intimidation.

EVENTS.h: Mortar blast kills at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency members in Zawiya
EVENTS.s: At least nine members of the Anti-Threat Security Agency, a force under the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity, were killed and several others wounded when an 82mm mortar round exploded during a training exercise in Zawiya late on Sunday, Libya Alahrar TV reported. Authorities made no immediate comment. Zawiya, about 40 km west of Tripoli and home to the country's largest operating refinery, has been the site of repeated clashes between rival armed groups.
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical and the trend is rising: on 22 October individuals entered the AGOCO crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and shut the valve on the Hamada-Tahara pipeline, cutting output at both fields (Reuters), the second forced pipeline closure in western Libya in five weeks; on 21 October armed men stormed the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose a disputed deputy head, drawing UNSMIL's strongest condemnation and a warning of targeted sanctions; and on 18 October an 82mm mortar blast killed at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency personnel during training in Zawiya (Reuters).

EVENTS.h: Ebola outbreak confirmed in eighth province, North Ubangi, on CAR border
EVENTS.s: Congo's public health institute confirmed that the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has spread to North Ubangi, the eighth affected province, after a series of deaths in a mining area of Wapinda health zone near the Central African Republic border. The outbreak has more than 9,000 confirmed cases and more than 4,000 deaths and is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. Insecurity in Ituri and North Kivu continues to hamper the response.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. Rating held at 4.

EVENTS.h: Two arrested for terrorism in Basque Country over security-force data and suspected arms cache
EVENTS.s: Basque regional police said on 18 October that a 34-year-old Spanish man and a 22-year-old Spanish woman were arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences following a search on 26 September. Items seized included information on security forces and the potential location of a site holding materials presumed to be weapons and explosives. Both will appear before Spain's National Court at a later date.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · weather recovery and protest watch. Spain's immediate risk remains environmental: Storm Adam killed four people in the Valencia region and Catalonia on 17-19 October, with 632 mm of rain in 36 hours at Pego, more than 2,000 evacuated and up to 800,000 people briefly under shelter-in-place orders; red alerts have been lifted but clean-up in Oliva, Pego, Els Poblets and the Marina Alta continues to disrupt secondary roads and commuter rail.

EVENTS.h: Petrol shortage spreads to Niamey; export ban in force, station tanks dry
EVENTS.s: Long queues formed at the few supplied stations in Niamey on 18 October after weeks of shortages in other towns, with station managers saying their tanks had been empty for four days, AFP reported. The Commerce Ministry banned petrol and diesel exports by decree on 12 October and the state oil company Sonidep must import petrol to cover domestic demand. The energy ministry recorded a deficit of 196.6 million litres of petrol over the first eight months of 2026.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · essential travel only with state-level clearance. The deadliest incident of the window struck the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen in three vehicles ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP), on the only corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic between Agadez and the uranium belt, and the military escort aboard did not prevent it.

EVENTS.h: Vehicle breaches Leipzig/Halle airport fence; north runway closed during search
EVENTS.s: German police said on 18 October they were investigating a breach at Leipzig/Halle airport where a vehicle appeared to have driven through a perimeter fence late on 17 October. Searches found no suspicious objects or unauthorised persons, but the north runway remained closed while checks continued. On 19 October police said two men had admitted breaking through the fence while one was practising for a driving test.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment hardened further this week: federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian national in Brandenburg on 22 October for gathering military intelligence for Russia, including on NATO eastern-flank sites and defence-industry production, one day after the Bundeswehr rated the Russian sabotage threat to its own forces as significant for the first time, citing the explosive-laden drone found near Wunstorf air base.

EVENTS.h: Nationwide cost-of-living riots: Limoges town hall burned, 3,000 shops hit, 2,400 arrested
EVENTS.s: Huge protests across France over the cost of living and underfunded public services on 17 October descended into riots and looting in some of the worst unrest in years. Limoges town hall was torched and more than 3,000 shops were pillaged or damaged according to the government, as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. Some 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend and partial curfews were organised in several municipalities.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning. France remains the epicentre of the European unrest wave: the 17 October riots torched Limoges town hall, damaged or looted more than 3,000 shops and put some 2,500 people in custody, and the government has responded with targeted night curfews in Paris, Lyon, Lille, Nice, Bordeaux and Marseille, protest bans in Paris, Lyon, Lille and Grenoble and troops alongside police for the Saturday 24 October protest day, which yellow-vest activists and the CGT union have joined.

EVENTS.h: Mine and gunfire on army patrol near Gamboru Ngala kill 10 soldiers, five CJTF
EVENTS.s: Troops from the Gamboru battalion patrolling the road between Gamboru Ngala and Cameroon on Saturday 17 October struck a landmine, killing eight soldiers instantly, two soldiers told Reuters. Gunmen then fired on a second vehicle, killing two more soldiers and five Civilian Joint Task Force members; six wounded soldiers were taken to Maimalari Military Hospital in Maiduguri. The mine was likely planted by Boko Haram.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja Ebola watch. The north-east is in its most dangerous phase in years: Boko Haram overran the army base at Guzamala on the night of 13 October, killing at least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard (Reuters, 15 Oct), and a mine-and-ambush attack on a patrol between Gamboru Ngala and the Cameroon border on 17 October killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF members (Reuters, 19 Oct); in the north-west, bandits killed at least 20 in a military-escorted traders' convoy in Bukkuyum, Zamfara, on 10 October (Reuters, 12 Oct), so armed escort cannot be treated as sufficient mitigation on rural roads.

EVENTS.adm: Bay region (Buurhakaba, Dinsoor, Berdale, Qansaxdheere, Awdiinle)
EVENTS.h: Forces loyal to ousted South West leader seize five Bay towns around Baidoa
EVENTS.s: Military officials said on 17 October that forces loyal to ousted South West State president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen had taken Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba and Qansaxdheere, plus Awdiinle about 30 km from Baidoa, leaving the federally backed administration without control of most of the state. Most takeovers were without resistance, but clashes were reported during the capture of Buurhakaba on the Mogadishu–Baidoa road; local officials fled to an AUSSOM base where Ethiopian troops did not intervene. South West Information Minister Nur Sidow Baba said the districts would be brought back under government control.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. As of 23 October, AFP-confirmed reporting shows Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces holding Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle (30 km from Baidoa), leaving Baidoa as the only major Bay town under the federally backed South West administration, which has vowed to retake the districts while Ethiopian AUSSOM troops stayed inside their bases; a fight for Baidoa remains the base case and the Mogadishu–Baidoa road through Buurhakaba is cut.

EVENTS.h: Student protests turn violent in Brussels and Liège; tear gas and water cannon
EVENTS.s: Several hundred mostly young people protested in central Brussels on 17 October against rising education costs, with rioters clashing with police in unrest partly inspired by demonstrations in France. Police used tear gas and water cannon and some protesters overturned a car. Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said what was unfolding was no longer mere protest; a parallel protest took place in Liège.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · strike and protest watch. Belgium remains the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: union strike days on 9 and 12 October disrupted Brussels Airport, rail, public transport and schools, and student-led protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, with police using tear gas and water cannon.

EVENTS.h: UGTT-led march of thousands is biggest anti-Saied protest in years
EVENTS.s: Thousands of Tunisians joined the largest protest against President Kais Saied in years on Saturday, led by the UGTT labour union and civil society groups, with hundreds of police deployed across the capital and roads around Habib Bourguiba Avenue closed. Protesters chanted 'The prisons are full, people are hungry!' and revived the 2011 slogan 'The people want the fall of the regime!'. The march passed without reported violence.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid central Tunis, Ettadhamen and Sfax-area flashpoints on protest days. Tunisia's risk profile is rising: on 22 October police fired tear gas at protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of Tunis, after the death of a man in custody, with parallel clashes in Jebeniana and Agareb in Sfax governorate and student protests in Sfax city (Reuters), five days after the UGTT-led march of 17 October, the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years.

EVENTS.h: Rubio warns troops surging on both sides of Ethiopia-Eritrea border risk broader conflict
EVENTS.s: Asked about the risk of war between Eritrea and Ethiopia, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on 17 October that troops were surging on both sides of the border following separatist attacks inside Ethiopia and the Ethiopian response, and that this could turn into a broader conflict. He said Washington had more communication than usual with Asmara in recent months and had lifted some small sanctions to improve links so it could act as a mediator.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea remains a party to the Tigray confrontation in all but name: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, Asmara asked the Council for Chapter VII deterrent measures against Ethiopia on 10 October, and Ethiopian troops reached Zalambessa on the border on 13 October.

EVENTS.h: Opposition wins Senate runoffs; Babiš's ANO takes no seats
EVENTS.s: Leading opposition parties won the most votes in Senate elections on 17 October, while Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's ANO failed to secure any of the seats it contested. The pro-European Mayors and Independents won 10 of the 14 seats they contested and the Civic Democrats seven. Babiš called the result catastrophic, but the outcome is unlikely to destabilise his coalition, which controls the lower house.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, violent unrest or major transport disruption was confirmed in Czechia between 9 and 23 October; the only notable event was the 17 October Senate runoff in which the opposition won and Babiš's ANO took no seats, with no incidents reported.

EVENTS.h: Army drone strike hits crowded Nyala livestock market
EVENTS.s: Sudan's army said it struck RSF command centres in Nyala on 16 October, while the RSF and its allies said a crowded livestock market was hit. The African Union Commission, citing local and medical sources, put the toll at 23 dead when it condemned the attack on 22 October. The UN says drone strikes are now the leading cause of civilian deaths in Sudan.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. The war is in a drone-dominated phase in which both sides strike far behind the front lines: AFP counted at least 80 dead when army drones hit a transport hub beside Al-Dibab market in West Kordofan on 18 October, AP and AFP reported a strike on central Nyala on 19 October that killed 17 and an RSF drone attack the same morning on a house east of Khartoum airport that killed four, and the army's 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market across the South Sudan border killed at least 153 by the Abyei administration's count.

EVENTS.h: Abiy names six-month Tigray caretaker government and calls for elections
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed named a caretaker administration to stabilise Tigray and prepare an election within six months, after the military and a pro-government militia took control of large parts of the region including Mekelle. His office said the administration would also repair infrastructure and help displaced people return; a TPLF spokesperson did not immediately comment. Around 750,000 Tigrayans were still internally displaced as of February, according to UNHCR.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Tigray is easing but not settled: federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa, Axum and Zalambessa, Al Jazeera reported shops and banks reopening in Mekelle on 22 October, and Abiy's six-month caretaker administration named on 16 October is preparing an election, yet the TPLF rejects it, the Ethiopia-Eritrea confrontation remains frozen with troops facing each other at Zalambessa and Rubio warned on 17 October that troop surges on both sides of the border could turn into a broader conflict.

EVENTS.h: EU approves nearly 32 million euros for Estonia's eastern-border drone surveillance
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Kristen Michal said at the European Council on 16 October that Estonia will receive nearly 32 million euros from the EU to strengthen drone surveillance along its eastern border. EU leaders also highlighted the Eastern Flank Watch project and agreed to restrict tourist visas for Russian nationals and step up sanctions pressure.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · do not cross into Russia from Narva. No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 9 and 23 October 2026; the most recent notable event remains the August arson attack on Milrem Robotics in Tallinn, which Tallinn attributed to Russian special services on 29 September.

EVENTS.h: Kinshasa bans 13 parties including Kabila's PPRD, calls FRN 'attack'
EVENTS.s: Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani ordered a nationwide ban on the activities of 13 political parties, including Kabila's PPRD, three days after the FRN launch. Government spokesman Patrick Muyaya said Kabila had formalised his attack against the Republic and that taking up arms meant killing Congolese to conquer territory. Opposition figures called the ban repression; the measure gives no duration or legal basis.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. Rating held at 4.

EVENTS.h: Electoral commission sets April–May 2027 polls; opposition rejects unilateral timetable
EVENTS.s: Somalia's National Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission announced on 15 October that parliamentary elections will be held on 15 April 2027 and the presidential vote on 15 May 2027, with party and voter registration from 1 to 22 November 2026. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term ended earlier this year and was extended by a constitutional amendment; the opposition, together with Puntland and Jubaland, rejected the schedule as one-sided, with critics warning it is a recipe for more conflict.
EVENTS.src: AFP (via Al Jazeera) and Reuters, 15 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. As of 23 October, AFP-confirmed reporting shows Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces holding Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle (30 km from Baidoa), leaving Baidoa as the only major Bay town under the federally backed South West administration, which has vowed to retake the districts while Ethiopian AUSSOM troops stayed inside their bases; a fight for Baidoa remains the base case and the Mogadishu–Baidoa road through Buurhakaba is cut.

EVENTS.h: EU grants Finland 32 million euros for Border Guard drone detection and counter-drone systems
EVENTS.s: The Ministry of the Interior announced on 15 October that Finland will receive 32 million euros from the EU Border Management and Visa Instrument to buy drone surveillance and counter-drone systems for the Border Guard. The systems are to improve drone monitoring on the eastern border and in the Gulf of Finland, with most procurements planned for 2027-2029.
EVENTS.src: Finnish Ministry of the Interior, 15 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid SE border zone during Russia strike nights. Finland is safe for travel and operations, but the south-eastern coast between Loviisa and the Russian border is subject to short-notice air and sea closures whenever Ukraine mounts large strikes on St Petersburg; the Defence Forces imposed such restrictions on three consecutive mornings on 16, 17 and 18 October, the last lasting from 02:45 to 09:43 during the record attack on St Petersburg, with no drones crossing into Finland.

EVENTS.h: Tsahkna warns Russia will step up hybrid attacks to erode Western support for Ukraine
EVENTS.s: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told Reuters at the Warsaw Security Forum on 15 October that the risk of Russia eroding Western support for Ukraine through hybrid attacks, sabotage and disinformation is a key concern for Estonia. European officials have warned that Moscow is intensifying such operations against NATO states.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · do not cross into Russia from Narva. No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 9 and 23 October 2026; the most recent notable event remains the August arson attack on Milrem Robotics in Tallinn, which Tallinn attributed to Russian special services on 29 September.

EVENTS.h: Istanbul's worst floods since 1942 kill at least four, thousands of properties damaged
EVENTS.s: Record rainfall on the night of 14 October flooded homes, businesses and streets across Istanbul; the interior minister called it the biggest flood disaster since 1942. AP reported four dead by 16 October, including a teenager who was electrocuted, with 9,850 damage reports filed and 46,000 personnel deployed. The toll later rose to eight, with about 2,000 homes and 900 businesses seriously damaged.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye in the 9-23 October window; the operational picture is dominated by the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight dead per AFP on 19 October) and by the political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October (Reuters), continuing detentions of opposition-run municipal officials, and Reuters-reported detention orders for 31 suspects in the investment-fund probe on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Roadside bomb kills Iraqi army brigadier and soldier south of Kirkuk
EVENTS.s: A roadside bomb killed an Iraqi army brigadier and a soldier and wounded two other soldiers about 80 km south of Kirkuk on 14 October as a patrol searched an Islamic State hideout struck by warplanes the day before. It was the second attack on security forces in the area this month after a 5 October attack claimed by Islamic State.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: a missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October (Reuters), the latest in a series of Iranian strikes on exile camps on 8, 12 and 17 October, and on 20 October Tehran's ambassador said Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups, a step Iraqi security officials had told AFP they refused.

EVENTS.h: Police raid opposition broadcaster Halk TV as government trustee appointed
EVENTS.s: Turkish authorities appointed a government trustee to run pro-opposition broadcaster Halk TV and police raided its Istanbul office, prosecutors said on 14 October. Live broadcasts were halted as part of an investigation into the channel's owner, extending a crackdown on critical media.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye in the 9-23 October window; the operational picture is dominated by the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight dead per AFP on 19 October) and by the political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October (Reuters), continuing detentions of opposition-run municipal officials, and Reuters-reported detention orders for 31 suspects in the investment-fund probe on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Five arrested in Norway over fraud and bribery on NATO ship contracts
EVENTS.s: Five people were arrested in Norway on 14 October and searches carried out in Germany and Romania in a Eurojust-coordinated probe into fraudulent invoicing and bribery linked to shore-support contracts for NATO vessels. Eurojust estimated losses to NATO member countries at around one million euros; Økokrim said the suspects were held in the Bergen area.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · heightened hybrid vigilance. Norway remains a low-risk operating environment; the only in-window events affecting movement were the heavily policed 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Støre and Stubb and Zelensky's 21 October visit to the Storting, both of which passed without incident.

EVENTS.h: US lifts sanctions on Assembly chief Jorge Rodríguez as third round of talks opens
EVENTS.s: The Trump administration removed Jorge Rodríguez, head of the National Assembly and brother of acting President Delcy Rodríguez, from the Treasury sanctions list on Wednesday. The notice came as he opened the third round of US-backed talks with an opposition faction on reforms to the top court and electoral council ahead of eventual elections. Caracas and Washington have a deal giving the US access to 17 oilfields.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · Caracas workable with advance; stand off from all demonstrations and party marches in central Caracas (Plaza Venezuela, Miraflores approaches), low profile, no overland border travel. The first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years passed on 22 October without wire-reported violence: thousands marched in Caracas, Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal and Maracaibo for a 2027 election date, Machado's return and the release of more than 320 political prisoners, with a thin security-force presence even as the ruling party held a rival march from the same square (Reuters, 22 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Boko Haram overruns Guzamala army base, killing at least 10 soldiers
EVENTS.s: Suspected Boko Haram fighters attacked the army base in Guzamala local government area on Tuesday night, overrunning troops, destroying military vehicles and setting fire to parts of nearby Mairari village, military sources told Reuters. At least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard were killed and more than 20 people wounded. The fighters seized more than 40 fishing boats at Tumbun Barebari before the assault.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja Ebola watch. The north-east is in its most dangerous phase in years: Boko Haram overran the army base at Guzamala on the night of 13 October, killing at least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard (Reuters, 15 Oct), and a mine-and-ambush attack on a patrol between Gamboru Ngala and the Cameroon border on 17 October killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF members (Reuters, 19 Oct); in the north-west, bandits killed at least 20 in a military-escorted traders' convoy in Bukkuyum, Zamfara, on 10 October (Reuters, 12 Oct), so armed escort cannot be treated as sufficient mitigation on rural roads.

EVENTS.h: MI5 chief: Iran targeting military sites, Russia 'aggressor number one'
EVENTS.s: MI5 Director General Ken McCallum said in his annual threat update that Iran is attempting to hit harder targets such as military sites and that Iran-linked operations led to more than 50 arrests in the past year, much of the activity aimed at Jewish communities. He called Russia aggressor number one and said state-threat casework has quadrupled in a decade. He said the RAF Fairford incident was not unique.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity.
