The UK picture through 23 October is dominated by state threats rather than street disorder: the RAF Fairford investigation moved on 20 October to National Security Act re-arrests for assisting Iranian intelligence, MI5 said on 13 October that Iran and Russia are both expanding hybrid campaigns and that Iran-linked operations produced more than 50 arrests in a year, and the Home Secretary set out new sanctions and powers on 12 October.

EVENTS.h: Slovakia restores military attachés with Russia for first time since 2022
EVENTS.s: Slovakia has restored military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, sending two military officers to Moscow while a Russian military attaché is expected in Bratislava. Prime Minister Robert Fico agreed the step with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin in May. The opposition and former senior officers warn of espionage risks and damage to trust within NATO.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, violent protest or transport disruption was confirmed in Slovakia between 9 and 23 October.

EVENTS.h: Ex-president Kabila launches FRN front, absorbing AFC/M23 rebellion
EVENTS.s: Joseph Kabila launched the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), a political-military coalition replacing the AFC/M23 alliance, at a press conference at his residence in rebel-held Goma. Rebel leaders Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki and Sultani Makenga will serve as his deputies, and the group says it will end 'tyranny' by all means including force. Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia last year for treason and is under US sanctions.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. Rating held at 4.

EVENTS.h: Second national strike day partly shuts public sector, rail and schools
EVENTS.s: Belgium's public sector was partially shut down on 12 October as unions staged a second day of nationwide strike action against planned budget cuts. Rail, public transport, public broadcasting and schools were affected. The action followed a mass protest in Brussels on 9 October that ended with a small group clashing with police, and came as coalition partners failed to agree a federal budget, forcing De Wever to cancel his State of the Union address.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · strike and protest watch. Belgium remains the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: union strike days on 9 and 12 October disrupted Brussels Airport, rail, public transport and schools, and student-led protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, with police using tear gas and water cannon.

EVENTS.h: Germany detains two Turkish suspects in Russia-linked Starlink station arson in Poland
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on 12 October that German police, at the request of Polish security services, had detained two Turkish citizens suspected of setting fire to a Starlink ground station in Wola Krobowska in September. Polish officials said the sabotage was carried out on behalf of Russian intelligence and that the suspects will face charges in Poland. The station provides satellite internet to Poland and other countries including Ukraine.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: three school stabbings in four days that killed a custodian and triggered checks of nearly 50,000 schools, German arrests on 12 October of two Turkish nationals suspected of the Russian-directed Starlink station arson near Warsaw, and the 19 October detention in Łódź of a Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course on spying suspicion.

EVENTS.h: Car bomb at El Bordo toll booth on Pan-American Highway injures three civilians
EVENTS.s: A car bomb exploded at a toll booth near El Bordo on Monday, injuring at least three civilians, the army said, blaming the FARC-dissident Carlos Patiño front. The same group killed an army sergeant in a clash in Timbío on Friday 9 October, and an ELN drone attack on a patrol in La Vega killed a soldier on Saturday 10 October. President de la Espriella called the toll-booth blast a terrorist attack on the highway.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Nariño, Catatumbo, Arauca; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali and overland travel on the Venezuelan border. President de la Espriella's government is escalating: a 22 October air strike on an ELN camp in El Tambo, Cauca killed nine guerrillas including the Southwestern War Front's military chief alias Marcos Pacífico (DW, 23 Oct), the fifth bombing of his term, three days after he ordered a 'total offensive' against the ELN and FARC dissidents from Arauca and demanded the ELN free five hostages including two CTI investigators (Presidencia, 19 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Home Secretary announces Iran sanctions, state-threats unit and base security
EVENTS.s: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood told Parliament the government is sanctioning two individuals involved in espionage and attacks on behalf of Iran in Europe and the US, has designated the IRGC under the National Security (State Threats) Act, and is building a specialist state-threats mission in Counter Terror Policing while tightening security around military bases. She said more than 23 people have been charged under the National Security Act since 2023.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity. The UK picture through 23 October is dominated by state threats rather than street disorder: the RAF Fairford investigation moved on 20 October to National Security Act re-arrests for assisting Iranian intelligence, MI5 said on 13 October that Iran and Russia are both expanding hybrid campaigns and that Iran-linked operations produced more than 50 arrests in a year, and the Home Secretary set out new sanctions and powers on 12 October.

EVENTS.h: Vienna prosecutors say journalist's spying arrest was unrelated to his job
EVENTS.s: The Vienna prosecutors' office said on 12 October that investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach was arrested because witnesses saw him observing the same location as two men suspected of spying, not because of his profession. Tkach and cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko were released without charge; Bondarenko was injured by glass from a car window during the arrest. The two other Ukrainians remain in investigative custody.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. Austria recorded no significant security incident between 9 and 23 October; the only notable event remains the Vienna counter-espionage case, in which two Ukrainians arrested on 5 October are held on suspicion of working for a foreign intelligence service, while two Ukrainska Pravda journalists detained on 8 October were released without charge and prosecutors said on 12 October the arrests were unrelated to their profession.

EVENTS.h: PAM agrees four-party coalition government with Istiqlal, USFP and PPS
EVENTS.s: The centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party, winner of the 23 September election, agreed on Monday to form a coalition government with three other parties. The parties said the deal 'produces a strong political government, made up of components marked by ideological and political proximity'. The cabinet was subsequently appointed by the King on 16 October.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · open for business. Morocco recorded no kinetic security incident between 9 and 23 October that a wire service confirmed; the environment remains political.

EVENTS.h: Algeria says it arrested 61 Moroccans suspected of preparing 'acts of sabotage'
EVENTS.s: The General Directorate of National Security announced on Sunday 11 October that 61 Moroccan nationals had been arrested earlier in the month on suspicion of planning 'acts of sabotage', referring to 'an international Moroccan criminal network' without detailing the plots. The suspects are said to have entered Algeria via mountain trails from Tunisia. The land border with Morocco has been closed since 1994 and diplomatic relations were severed in 2021.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · southern and eastern border zones restricted. No terrorist attack, clash or significant protest was wire-confirmed in Algeria for 9-23 October; the environment is stable but heavily securitised and the state continues to frame domestic problems as foreign-backed subversion.

EVENTS.h: Air strikes on Sudan-border gold mine kill at least 72, rights group says
EVENTS.s: At least 72 workers were killed in air strikes on the Jabal al-Uqaydat gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border on Saturday, Sudan's Emergency Lawyers rights group said on 11 October, accusing the Egyptian air force; AFP could not independently verify the account and Egypt issued no comment. Survivors told AFP a jet struck five times at around 8am with thousands of people at the site. It was the second strike this year on the site after one in June that killed 23, which the Egyptian army said was an operation 'within Egyptian territory' against illegal gold mining and arms smuggling.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · Red Sea/Suez watch; North Sinai and Sudan border restricted. No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was wire-confirmed in Egypt for 9-23 October, but the external-security profile is rising.

EVENTS.h: Third school attack in a week; custodian killed earlier, 76 detained in nationwide sweep
EVENTS.s: A 21-year-old woman wounded three people with a dangerous object at a post-secondary school in Warsaw's Praga district on 10 October, the third attack at a Polish school in less than a week; none of the injuries was life-threatening. On 7 October a 19-year-old injured nine people at a vocational school in Masovia and on 8 October a 15-year-old killed a school custodian and wounded two others at his former school. Police said they detained 76 people and checked nearly 50,000 schools nationwide to prevent further violence.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: three school stabbings in four days that killed a custodian and triggered checks of nearly 50,000 schools, German arrests on 12 October of two Turkish nationals suspected of the Russian-directed Starlink station arson near Warsaw, and the 19 October detention in Łódź of a Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course on spying suspicion.

EVENTS.h: Eritrea asks UNSC for Chapter VII deterrent measures against Ethiopia
EVENTS.s: Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on 10 October to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia under Chapter VII of the UN Charter, in a letter from Foreign Minister Osman Saleh seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusation of an Eritrean invasion amounted to a declaration of war. Ethiopia had written to the Council a day earlier accusing Eritrea of an all-out invasion of Tigray; Asmara denies any incursion.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea remains a party to the Tigray confrontation in all but name: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, Asmara asked the Council for Chapter VII deterrent measures against Ethiopia on 10 October, and Ethiopian troops reached Zalambessa on the border on 13 October.

EVENTS.h: Intercommunal street battles in Rumbek kill 71 before security forces regain control
EVENTS.s: Clashes between rival armed communities erupted inside Rumbek town, the capital of Lakes State, on 9 October after outsiders attempted to take control of parts of the town. The government's preliminary report put the death toll at about 71 and said it was expected to rise; security forces regained control of the town.
EVENTS.impl: No-go outside Juba · essential travel only. South Sudan is absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October strike on Amiet market in Abyei, which hit a fuel depot and which a Sudanese military officer told AP targeted RSF-bound fuel tankers, killed at least 153 by the Abyei administration's count given to Reuters and AP and displaced about 8,000; UNISFA said on 21 October that many remain missing and the toll is expected to rise.

EVENTS.h: Overcrowded migrant boat sinks off Obock; at least 139 dead, 84 missing
EVENTS.s: A boat carrying about 305 people, mostly Ethiopian migrants heading for Yemen and the Arabian Peninsula, capsized off Godoria north of Obock on the night of 8-9 October. The UN migration agency IOM said on 11 October that the death toll had risen to 139 with 84 still missing and 82 survivors rescued. More than 900 migrants died or went missing on the route in 2025.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · transit hub. No violent security incident was recorded inside Djibouti in the past 14 days; the major event remains the 8-9 October migrant shipwreck off Obock (139 dead and 84 missing per IOM), while UNHCR counted 3,836 refugees arrived from Yemen in Obock region by 17 October with an acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in the Markazi camp.

EVENTS.h: Masked rioters clash with police at Brussels anti-austerity march during national strike
EVENTS.s: Violent rioters, many of them masked, confronted police at the edge of a large anti-austerity march in Brussels on 9 October during a national strike against the De Wever government's planned budget cuts. Police responded with water cannon and tear gas in the central tourist district. The strike disrupted public transport and flights at Brussels Airport.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · strike and protest watch. Belgium remains the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: union strike days on 9 and 12 October disrupted Brussels Airport, rail, public transport and schools, and student-led protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, with police using tear gas and water cannon.

EVENTS.h: Police kill man who held 13 children at knifepoint in Curitiba school
EVENTS.s: A man who climbed into the CMEI São Braz school and held 13 children and staff hostage at knifepoint for more than two hours was killed by Paraná state police on Friday. He had poured a liquid smelling of petrol in the classroom and threatened to set it alight; none of the children were injured. Police said the suspect suffered from schizophrenia.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct; avoid favela-adjacent routes, Avenida Brasil at night and election-day crowds; expect result-related gatherings in Brasília, São Paulo and Rio on Sunday night. Brazil votes on Sunday 25 October in a presidential runoff that Quaest (Reuters, 21 Oct) puts at 45-44 for Flávio Bolsonaro over Lula, within the margin of error, and on 20-21 October each camp filed a petition at the Superior Electoral Court to disqualify the other (AFP, 22 Oct), so a narrow result is likely to be contested in court and on the street.

EVENTS.h: Four Ukrainians arrested in Vienna on suspicion of spying; journalist released
EVENTS.s: Interior Minister Gerhard Karner said on 9 October that four Ukrainians had been arrested in Vienna that week on suspicion of spying, with three remaining in custody at the time. Ukrainska Pravda said its investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach was released after more than 12 hours and that cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko was injured during detention. Two men arrested on 5 October are suspected of working for a Ukrainian intelligence service.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. Austria recorded no significant security incident between 9 and 23 October; the only notable event remains the Vienna counter-espionage case, in which two Ukrainians arrested on 5 October are held on suspicion of working for a foreign intelligence service, while two Ukrainska Pravda journalists detained on 8 October were released without charge and prosecutors said on 12 October the arrests were unrelated to their profession.

ADVS.t: Nigeria — first Ebola case in Abuja: screening and evacuation cover
ADVS.b: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on 20 October: a Ugandan woman who arrived in Abuja via Addis Ababa on 5 October, fell ill two days later and was treated at a private hospital before being tested on 19 October (Reuters, AP, DW); on 21 October the NCDC confirmed the Bundibugyo strain and said the patient had deteriorated into multi-organ failure, and on 22 October the health minister said there was no evidence of community spread (Reuters). Authorities are tracing 44 contacts, most of them healthcare workers; there is no approved vaccine or treatment for this species, and the outbreak has killed more than 4,600 people since May. No travel restrictions are in force and the security picture in Abuja and Lagos is unchanged.
pts: Confirm medical-evacuation cover and the receiving facility for every principal in Abuja and Lagos before travel; private hospitals in Abuja are the exposure point so far
Brief principals on symptom reporting and avoiding non-essential clinic visits; carry a 72-hour medical kit
Expect entry screening and possible route changes at Nnamdi Azikiwe and Murtala Muhammed airports; build slack into transfers
Trigger for posture review: any secondary case, a healthcare-worker infection, or a case outside Abuja

ADVS.t: Western Europe — protest, curfew and strike disruption (France, Italy, Belgium)
ADVS.b: Current as of 23 October 2026. France keeps targeted night curfews in Paris (République and Les Halles, to 26 October), Lyon, Lille, Nice, Bordeaux and Marseille after the 17 October cost-of-living marches turned to rioting (some 2,500 taken into custody, 174 jailed), troops are assigned static roles for the 24 October protest day, and although a Paris administrative court overturned the prefecture's protest ban on 22 October and thousands rallied peacefully, Macron said the general rule for the coming days is no demonstrations and marches in Lyon, Marseille and Montpellier for Saturday are banned (AP, 22 Oct); Milan saw two days of rioting and looting (271 detained), a 20 October cabinet decree sends 500 troops to the city to year-end and the 17 October movement has called rallies for 24 October in Milan, Florence, Bologna, Turin, Rome and Naples; Belgian education and budget protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, budget talks failed again on 21 October and a deal is now expected next week. Haulier blockades that emptied shelves and pumps in southern Italy began to lift in Sicily and Calabria on 22 October after the cabinet approved a diesel-aid decree (Reuters, 22 Oct); confirm fuel and road status before routing through Campania and Calabria.
pts: Check curfew hours and protest calendars before any evening movement in Paris, Milan, Turin, Rome or Brussels
Pre-book ground transport and build a 24-hour slip into itineraries through Brussels and Italian hubs on announced strike days
Screen venue-adjacent accommodation for protest-zone exposure; avoid city-centre squares on announced march days
Fuel: full tanks before entering southern Italy until roadblocks are fully cleared; confirm aviation-fuel status before booking into Calabrian regional airports

ADVS.b: Current as of 23 October 2026. Al-Shabaab activity in the capital is at its lowest level in years and is now low-lethality harassment of checkpoints on the western (Afgooye-corridor) districts, mostly overnight; no large or complex attack in Mogadishu or at the airport was wire-reported between 9 and 23 October. The threats that reach the airport enclave are different: indirect fire — seven mortar barrages on AAIA and Halane between January 2024 and May 2025, one of them lethal, none since — and government–opposition confrontation, which reached the AAIA perimeter in June 2026 and is building again: the federal government has lost most of South West State to forces loyal to the ousted regional president, who hold Buurhakaba on the Mogadishu–Baidoa road (AFP, 17 Oct), and set a contested April–May 2027 election timetable that Puntland, Jubaland and the opposition reject (AFP/Reuters, 15 Oct).
pts: Movement limited to the AAIA/Halane enclave and the airport road, with contracted armed advance; no movement into Hodan, Daynile or the Afgooye corridor
Indirect-fire drills and hard cover current for every principal in the enclave; last barrage cadence was four in nine weeks (Apr–May 2025)
In-place plan that does not depend on the airport road being open, with 72 hours of self-sufficiency
Trigger for posture review: armed convoys entering Wadajir or Waaberi, security forces surrounding opposition residences, or any mortar fire anywhere in Banaadir
Sanctions screening re-run on any counterparty with South West State or Laftagareen links

ADVS.b: Current as of 23 October 2026. Mali (ISSP killing of at least 48 civilians in Ménaka, 18–19 Oct), Niger (gunmen killed at least 11 on two escorted passenger buses outside Agadez, 20 Oct), Sudan (drone strikes killing at least 80 in West Kordofan on 18 Oct and 17 in Nyala on 19 Oct), South Sudan (at least 153 reported killed at Abyei's Amiet market, 19 Oct), northern Ethiopia and Eritrea (federal–TPLF settlement contested, troops facing each other at Zalambessa, and Oromia–Somali regional fighting at Moyale on 21–22 Oct pushing hundreds into Kenya) and eastern DRC remain outside the TCG movement envelope. Requirements in these jurisdictions are referred, not accepted, unless a dedicated advance and armed local capability are contracted in writing.
pts: No principal movement without contracted local armed support
Written client acknowledgement of residual risk before mobilisation
Medical evacuation route confirmed and funded before deployment — Djibouti and Nairobi remain the staging assumption
Sanctions screening on every local counterparty

ADVS.t: Kurdistan Region — drone threat to Erbil and flight contingency
ADVS.b: Four Iranian strikes in two weeks on Iranian Kurdish opposition sites in Erbil province — drones on 8, 12 and 17 Oct, and a missile at a camp north-east of the city on 21 Oct (Reuters) — plus an explosion at a PMF headquarters in Baghdad (17 Oct) and Iraq's closure of the Sheeb crossing with Iran for a security review (21 Oct). Tehran says Baghdad has agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups (AFP, 20 Oct); no further strike was wire-reported on 22–23 Oct. With coalition air defences gone since the 30 September US withdrawal, commercial schedules into Erbil remain exposed to short-notice airspace closures.
pts: Build a 24-hour slip into inbound itineraries
Confirm ground assets independently of flight status
Avoid the western and north-eastern approaches to Erbil (Koya, Zrgwez and Balisan camp areas) where strikes have landed
Brief principals on overland alternatives via Türkiye before departure

ADVS.t: Russia and the Baltic–Nordic frontier — hybrid and deep-strike exposure
ADVS.b: Russia: largest drone attack yet on St Petersburg (18 Oct, one killed, oil terminal ablaze), 630 drones sent towards Moscow overnight on 21–22 Oct with apartment blocks hit in Lipetsk (Reuters), all four Moscow airports closed up to seven hours (16 Oct), and a Swedish national arrested by the FSB on sabotage charges (15 Oct) — detention risk for Western nationals is arbitrary, and the 21 Oct release of American Stephen Hubbard during the Witkoff talks shows detainees are traded as diplomatic currency. Finland closed Gulf of Finland air and sea zones on Russian strike nights (16 and 18 Oct); an Estonian ex-soldier is held by the FSB after crossing from Narva.
pts: Russia is no-go for TCG principals; no overland crossings from Narva or the Finnish south-east
Expect short-notice closures of Finnish and Estonian coastal airspace on Russian strike nights
Treat GPS degradation as standard in the Gulf of Finland and eastern Baltic
Brief dual nationals and anyone with prior military service on arbitrary-detention exposure

ADVS.t: Kenya — Ebola screening and Level 3 advisory
ADVS.b: The United States raised Kenya to Level 3 (reconsider travel) on 19 October over Ebola, crime and terrorism; Kenya confirmed a ninth Ebola case on 20 October, all nine in one cluster of relatives and healthcare workers detected in quarantine, with no community transmission reported. On 21–22 October fighting between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional forces in Moyale sent hundreds of Ethiopians across the border and stray rounds wounded a woman and struck a police officer on the Kenyan side (AP, Reuters). Nairobi remains the regional hub and staging node.
pts: Health screening and medical-evacuation cover confirmed for every principal transiting Nairobi
No movement into Garissa, Mandera, Wajir or Lamu counties, or to Moyale and the Marsabit border strip while the Ethiopian fighting continues
Brief principals against unvetted ride-hailing and after-dark solo movement in Nairobi

OUTLOOK.a: Core Europe faces two overlapping stressors over the next 90 days. The cost-of-living and education unrest that produced the 17 October riots in France and Italy and clashes in Belgium is now being met with curfews, protest bans, troop deployments and new criminal offences; the 24 October protest day in France and Italy, the 5 November French national strike, the 11 November Spanish general strike and Belgium's unresolved budget will test whether the state response contains or inflames it, and a repeat of 17 October-scale violence in any one city would push that country to a higher rating. In parallel, the Russian hybrid campaign is escalating in intensity and lethality, with Germany rating the sabotage threat to its forces as significant, a GRU-linked arrest in Brandenburg, Starlink arsons in Poland and Bulgaria, and Tusk warning of larger provocations before Christmas; the UK adds an Iranian state-threat layer aimed at US-linked bases and Jewish sites. Expect periodic airport, rail and city-centre disruption rather than mass-casualty attacks, with the greatest uncertainty in France and southern Italy.
dr: Cost-of-living and education protests in France, Italy and Belgium meeting hard-line policing, curfews and protest bans ahead of scheduled strike and rally days
Escalating Russian sabotage and espionage against defence, logistics and Ukraine-linked infrastructure in Germany, Poland and neighbouring states
Iranian state-threat activity in the UK against US-linked military sites and Jewish community targets, with National Security Act investigations ongoing
ind: Scale, arrests and injuries on the 24 October protest day in France and Italy, and whether curfews and protest bans are extended beyond 26 October
New drone, arson or explosive incidents at airports, rail hubs, military sites or Starlink and defence facilities in Germany, Poland or Czechia
Belgian budget outcome and union strike calls, the 5 November French strike, and the 29 October Renfe and 11 November general strikes in Spain
OUTLOOK.im: Journey management in France and Italy should treat Saturdays and announced strike days as no-go windows for city centres and build curfew-aware, fuel-resilient routing for southern Italy, while security teams across the region should raise protective posture around airports, rail hubs and defence-linked client sites in line with the German and Polish sabotage warnings.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the region's risk picture will be driven by Ukraine's deep-strike campaign against St Petersburg and Moscow and Russia's response, with Finland's south-eastern coast and the Baltic approaches experiencing recurring short-notice air and sea closures each time a major raid is mounted; three consecutive closure mornings on 16-18 October show the tempo is rising into winter. Russia itself stays no-go, with record drone volumes, unreliable air travel and continued use of detained Westerners as bargaining chips even as US-mediated trilateral talks are pencilled in for November. Norway, Finland and Estonia remain workable, but the hybrid threat to critical infrastructure, defence firms and sanctions-enforcement actors is the principal watch item, and Russian propaganda accusing Estonia of guiding drone attacks on St Petersburg raises the risk of retaliatory pressure on the Narva border. Any ceasefire framework from the November talks could ease strike tempo quickly, but a breakdown would likely bring larger raids and more frequent closures.
dr: Ukrainian long-range drone campaign against St Petersburg, Moscow and Russian energy infrastructure, and the resulting Finnish air and sea closures in the eastern Gulf of Finland
Outcome of US-mediated trilateral talks expected in November following Witkoff's Oslo and St Petersburg meetings
Russian hybrid activity against Nordic-Baltic critical infrastructure, defence industry and sanctions enforcement, including coastal espionage from civilian vessels
ind: Frequency and duration of Finnish Defence Forces restricted areas off Kotka and Loviisa, and any confirmed drone crossing into Finnish or Estonian airspace
New FSB arrests of Western nationals in Russia and the handling of remaining detainees around the November talks
Sabotage, arson or cyber incidents against Estonian, Finnish or Norwegian infrastructure or defence firms, and Russian measures at the Narva or Storskog crossings
OUTLOOK.im: Keep Russia at no-go with independent exit routes via the Baltics, and brief clients transiting south-eastern Finland and the Gulf of Finland to expect multi-hour air and sea closures with little notice on nights of major Ukrainian strikes; Nordic-Baltic capitals remain routine for travel with heightened vigilance for hybrid incidents.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the Kurdistan Region faces continued Iranian drone and missile strikes on exile camps in Erbil province, now unanswered since coalition air defences left with the 30 September US withdrawal, and growing Tehran pressure on Baghdad to expel the opposition groups; Islamic State sleeper cells remain active in the Kirkuk belt. Reported US-Israeli planning for renewed strikes on Iran after the US midterms would sharply raise the risk of militia retaliation on Erbil and Baghdad and of airspace closures. Türkiye is stable at the security level, with the PKK dissolution holding, but the media and municipal crackdown, planned press-freedom protests, the Imamoglu trial and COP31 in Antalya in November will drive recurrent demonstrations and heavy policing.
dr: Iranian strikes on Kurdish exile camps in Erbil province with no coalition air defence since 30 September
US-Israeli preparations for renewed strikes on Iran and the risk of Iraqi militia retaliation
Türkiye's political crackdown on opposition media and municipalities ahead of the Imamoglu trial and COP31
ind: Any strike or drone interception inside Erbil city or near Erbil airport, or a US Mission airspace alert
Baghdad formally acting on the expulsion or disarmament of Iranian Kurdish groups
Turnout and policing at the 24 October press-freedom demonstrations and Imamoglu trial hearings
OUTLOOK.im: Keep Erbil at essential-travel-with-advance with contingency routing via Sulaimaniyah or overland to Türkiye, and plan Istanbul and Ankara movements around announced demonstrations and court dates.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days North Africa's risk is driven from its edges rather than its core: Libya's armed groups are again using infrastructure seizures (Hamada-Tahara valve, Audit Bureau raid) as leverage while the UN track inches forward, Tunisia has moved from peaceful mass protest to localised violent unrest within a week, and Egypt's 26 October vote on military support for Saudi Arabia could draw Houthi retaliation towards Egyptian and Suez-linked targets. Morocco and Algeria remain kinetically quiet but locked in an escalating diplomatic confrontation that will peak around the 31 October MINURSO renewal. No change in country ratings is warranted today, but Tunisia is the most likely candidate for an upgrade to High if custody-death protests spread beyond Tunis suburbs and Sfax.
dr: Libyan armed-group leverage over oil infrastructure and sovereign institutions in the west, with UNSMIL mandate renewal due 31 October
Tunisian economic distress and the Saied crackdown converting peaceful UGTT mobilisation into street clashes
Egypt's prospective defensive deployment to Saudi Arabia and Houthi threats against Egyptian stability and Red Sea shipping
ind: Reopening or escalation of the Hamada-Tahara valve closure, and any armed response to the Audit Bureau raid in Tripoli
Further custody-death or service-failure protests in Tunisian cities and any UGTT general-strike call
Outcome of Egypt's 26 October parliamentary vote and any Houthi claim against Egyptian or Suez-linked assets
OUTLOOK.im: Keep Libya at essential-only with armed escort and air-evacuation plans, add Ettadhamen and Sfax-governorate flashpoints to Tunisia journey plans alongside central Tunis, and pre-position Red Sea and Suez contingency routing in case Egypt's vote triggers Houthi retaliation.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the central Sahel will remain the most lethal theatre in the region: ISSP's Menaka massacre and its open war with JNIM on the Mali-Burkina-Niger borders mean civilians and anyone tied to the state face reprisal killings, while JNIM's fuel blockade of Bamako and the Malian junta's dependence on Africa Corps drone strikes ensure the conflict keeps generating both insurgent attacks and civilian-harm incidents. In Niger, the Agadez bus ambush shows that the northern mining corridor is no longer insulated from mass-casualty violence, and the fuel shortage in Niamey adds civil-unrest and movement risk to an already coup-prone regime. In Nigeria, Boko Haram and ISWAP have inflicted their heaviest losses on the army in months in Borno, bandit ambushes on escorted convoys continue in Zamfara, and the Abuja Ebola case introduces a public-health variable whose trajectory over the next three weeks will determine whether screening and movement restrictions affect the capital's air links.
dr: ISSP-JNIM rivalry and ISSP reprisals against communities in Menaka and Tillaberi, alongside JNIM's blockade strategy around Bamako
Boko Haram/ISWAP offensive momentum against army bases and patrols in Borno and persistent bandit control of rural roads in Zamfara and Kaduna
Fuel scarcity and junta fragility in Niger and Mali after the failed August mutiny in Niamey and the April offensive in Mali
ind: Further ISSP or JNIM attacks on escorted convoys or towns in Menaka, Gao and northern Niger, or a renewed assault on Bamako or Niamey
Secondary Ebola transmission in Abuja or new airport screening and attestation requirements for passengers to and from Nigeria
Fuel riots, curfews or a change of leadership in Niamey, and whether Bamako fuel convoys continue to get through
OUTLOOK.im: Mali and Niger stay no-go for Western corporate travel; in Nigeria, journey management should treat military escort as insufficient on rural roads in the north-east and north-west, keep Abuja programmes under daily Ebola review and ensure medical-evacuation cover is confirmed before travel.

OUTLOOK.a: Somalia: As of 23 October, AFP-confirmed reporting shows Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces holding Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle (30 km from Baidoa), leaving Baidoa as the only major Bay town under the federally backed South West administration, which has vowed to retake the districts while Ethiopian AUSSOM troops stayed inside their bases; a fight for Baidoa remains the base case and the Mogadishu–Baidoa road through Buurhakaba is cut. The electoral commission's 15 October timetable (parliament 15 April, president 15 May 2027) is rejected by the opposition, Puntland and Jubaland, sustaining the risk of armed political confrontation in Mogadishu, and IOM now projects up to 874,000 flood displacements by December with the Shabelle rising at Jowhar and the Juba at Dollow, which will degrade road movement in Hiraan, Middle Shabelle and Gedo. No large or complex al-Shabaab attack in the capital or at Aden Adde airport was wire-reported between 9 and 23 October; rating 4 and rising trend are retained and posture remains no-go outside the airport/Halane enclave, with Bay and Bakool regions and the Mogadishu–Baidoa road closed. Over the next 90 days the region's two wars will keep setting the baseline: Sudan's drone campaign has produced its bloodiest fortnight of the year (Al-Dibab, Nyala, Khartoum, Abyei) and has now crossed into South Sudan and Chad with no ceasefire track after the 21 October Geneva meeting, so expect further mass-casualty strikes on markets, fuel points and supply corridors in Kordofan, Darfur, Abyei and along the borders. In Ethiopia the Tigray front is easing under federal control, but the Ethiopia-Eritrea standoff at Zalambessa is frozen rather than resolved, the Amhara insurgency persists and the Oromia-Somali clash in Moyale shows how quickly secondary fronts can open on Kenya's border. Kenya's Ebola cluster has so far stayed inside quarantine, which keeps Nairobi workable, while Djibouti's exposure is driven by the Houthi push for Yemen's Red Sea coast rather than anything inside the country. The dry season from November will widen armed movement in South Sudan and raise the risk of an Ethiopia-Eritrea miscalculation.
dr: Drone warfare by both SAF and RSF against civilian gatherings and fuel supply lines, now spilling into Abyei, South Sudan and Chad
Ethiopia-Eritrea confrontation at the Tigray border with severed ties, duelling UN Security Council letters and Abiy's sea-access ambitions
Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and the wider US-Israel-Iran conflict pressing on Bab el-Mandeb shipping and Djibouti-based forces
ind: Any Ethiopian or Eritrean ground movement across the Zalambessa line, or drone strikes on Eritrean territory
Further SAF or RSF strikes on Abyei, Khartoum airport or the eastern dams, or an RSF push from Kordofan toward El Obeid
A Kenyan Ebola case outside the quarantined cluster, or Moyale fighting spreading into Marsabit county
OUTLOOK.im: Sudan, South Sudan outside Juba and northern Ethiopia remain no-go for client travel; Nairobi, Addis Ababa and Djibouti City are workable with health screening and advance planning, but journey managers should hold evacuation options under review given the speed with which the Abyei, Moyale and Ebola situations developed inside a single week.

OUTLOOK.a: Kabila's open assumption of the rebellion's leadership turns the eastern insurgency into an explicit bid for national power and has pushed Kinshasa into a repressive reflex (party bans, Higher Defence Council, travel restrictions on officers) that raises the risk of politically driven unrest and arbitrary detention in the capital over the next 90 days. The Doha and Washington frameworks survive on paper, with the FRN claiming the AFC's commitments and the AU and Belgium calling for the ceasefire to be respected, but fighting with drones and artillery continues along the Walungu-Kamanyola, Minembwe and Masisi-Walikale axes and neither side is deterred. The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, now in eight provinces with over 9,700 confirmed cases and a near-50 percent case fatality ratio, will keep complicating access and medical evacuation across the east and the north, and exported cases in Kenya and Nigeria increase the chance of further regional travel restrictions. Expect the Kivus and Ituri to remain no-go, Kinshasa to remain workable but volatile, and the government to tighten controls on opposition and civic activity ahead of the constitutional-reform fight.
dr: Kabila-led FRN consolidating M23/AFC and Twirwaneho under one command with Rwandan backing
Kinshasa's hardening response: party bans, treason framing, and third-term constitutional push fuelling opposition anger
Ebola spread beyond the Kivus/Ituri into Haut-Uele, Tshopo and the Ubangis amid attacks on the response
ind: FRN/M23 offensive toward Kamanyola, Uvira or Walikale, or any strike on Bukavu-Uvira road traffic
Arrests of PPRD or other banned-party figures in Kinshasa, or dispersal of C64 protests with live fire
New Ebola health zones in Kinshasa-bound corridors (Tshopo, Equateur) or additional exported cases triggering regional border closures
OUTLOOK.im: Keep all North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri travel suspended and Kinshasa movements on advance-notified, low-profile itineraries with contingency for sudden internet, road or airport restrictions; Ebola screening and medevac constraints should be built into every eastern and northern DRC plan.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the region's risk is political rather than kinetic for travellers: Brazil's runoff on 25 October is a statistical tie with disqualification petitions already lodged by both camps, so a narrow result will be litigated and could draw street mobilisation in Brasília, São Paulo and Rio into November. Colombia will keep escalating under de la Espriella's 'total offensive', with air strikes every two to three weeks and guerrilla retaliation concentrated on the Pan-American Highway in Cauca and Nariño, Catatumbo and Arauca rather than in the main cities. Venezuela's transition is moving slowly through US-sponsored talks while the Machado-aligned opposition shifts to street pressure for an election date; the 22 October protest was peaceful and lightly policed, but no date exists and each future mobilisation carries a risk of a harder response.
dr: Brazil runoff result margin and the Superior Electoral Court's handling of the two disqualification petitions
Colombian air strikes and the ELN/FARC-dissident retaliation cycle on highways and against security forces in Cauca, Nariño, Catatumbo and Arauca
Pace of Venezuela's US-backed talks and whether an election date is set before the opposition escalates street pressure
ind: Post-runoff protests or road blockades in Brazil, and any TSE ruling on candidate disqualification
Attacks on toll plazas, pipelines or military posts within 72 hours of each Colombian bombing; ELN armed-strike announcements
Arrests at opposition marches in Caracas, a cabinet change involving Interior Minister Cabello, or an announced election timetable
OUTLOOK.im: Hold Rio and Brasília at elevated through at least 27 October and pre-position for result-driven demonstrations; keep Colombian itineraries to air travel between Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena with no road movement in Cauca, Nariño, Catatumbo or Arauca; in Caracas treat every announced march as a stand-off event and keep border travel closed.

AAIA.s: On a Sunday afternoon a suicide car bomb was driven into the gate of the Elite Hotel on Lido Beach, a popular weekend venue for Mogadishu's politicians and business community, and a small team of gunmen then stormed the building. Security forces fought room to room for roughly seven hours before the last attacker was killed. The UN later put the toll at at least 17 dead. The attack re-established the Al-Shabaab 'gate VBIED then assault team' template against soft, high-status venues that would recur through 2024.

AAIA.tg: Hotel near AAIA used by officials and officers
AAIA.s: A car bomb detonated at the entrance of Hotel Afrik, on the main road between the city and the airport, and four gunmen fought their way inside. The siege lasted several hours; among the dead was a retired Somali general. Civilians trapped in the hotel were rescued by security forces, and the UN Special Representative condemned the attack the next day. The venue's location — on the airport approach and within sight of the Halane access route — made it the closest hotel-siege to AAIA in the period.

AAIA.tg: Civilians and soldiers at a checkpoint
AAIA.s: A suicide bomber wearing an explosive vest walked into a corrugated-tin teashop beside a government security checkpoint in Wadajir, the district that physically borders both the airport and the AU mission headquarters, and detonated among off-duty soldiers and civilians. At least 11 people were killed. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack; the prime minister condemned it as a 'barbaric act'. It illustrates the group's use of low-cost person-borne devices against checkpoint clusters on the airport's landward side.

AAIA.tg: AU convoy (claimed); school and civilians hit
AAIA.s: At 07:30 a suicide bomber in an SUV detonated beside a passing convoy on a busy Hodan road just as pupils were arriving at the neighbouring Mocaasir Primary and Secondary School. Al-Shabaab said the target was an AU Mission convoy; the blast instead killed eight people and injured 17, including teachers and children, and heavily damaged the school. The incident is a reminder that convoy-targeted VBIEDs on the KM4–airport axis produce heavy collateral casualties in the dense districts between the city centre and AAIA.

A suicide car bomber rammed a convoy on the main road leading to the AAIA/Halane entrance, killing around eight people. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack and said it targeted a convoy carrying Western contractors and security staff. The strike demonstrated the vulnerability of the single approach road that all airport and Halane traffic must use, and prompted a tightening of convoy procedures for the compound.

Gunmen penetrated the eastern area of Aden Adde International Airport and attacked a military position inside the perimeter; black smoke was visible near the runway during the firefight. Five people, including an AMISOM soldier, were killed before the two attackers were shot. The assault was coordinated with twin suicide bombings in Beledweyne the same day that killed dozens, including a federal MP. It remains the only confirmed ground penetration of the AAIA perimeter in the period and exposed gaps on the airfield's eastern (beach-side) edge.

AAIA.tg: Hotel used by officials and businessmen
AAIA.s: Two car bombs breached the Hayat Hotel's defences on a Friday evening and a team of gunmen barricaded themselves inside with hostages. Security forces took around 30 hours to clear the building floor by floor; 21 people were killed and over 100 injured, many by the second blast that hit responders and bystanders. It was the first major Mogadishu attack after President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's 2022 election and triggered his declaration of 'total war' on Al-Shabaab.
AAIA.src: Widely reported; 30-hour siege referenced at thedefensepost.com/2025/04/06

AAIA.s: At around 14:00 a vehicle bomb exploded at the Zobe junction outside the Ministry of Education; minutes later a second VBIED detonated as ambulances and crowds converged, destroying at least one ambulance. More than 120 people were killed and over 300 injured — the deadliest attack in Somalia since the October 2017 truck bomb at the same junction. Al-Shabaab admitted responsibility on 1 November, framing the ministry as a legitimate target. The sequenced 'second blast on first responders' tactic is the defining feature of this event.

AAIA.loc: Villa Rose Hotel, Bondhere (near Villa Somalia)
AAIA.tg: Hotel frequented by ministers and MPs
AAIA.s: Gunmen stormed the Villa Rose Hotel, a short walk from the presidential palace and a known residence for ministers, after a car bomb at the gate. The siege lasted roughly 20 hours; around nine people were killed and the environment minister was among the wounded. The attack showed Al-Shabaab's willingness to strike inside the government district despite the heightened security that followed the October Zobe bombing.

A bomb exploded in the Pearl Beach hotel restaurant on a Friday evening and seven gunmen then entered the building, taking diners hostage. Security forces freed 84 people during an overnight operation and killed all seven attackers; six civilians and three soldiers died. The attack repeated the 2020 Elite Hotel pattern on the same stretch of Lido Beach, underlining that beachfront leisure venues 4–5 km from AAIA remain a preferred soft target.

Several mortar rounds were fired into the airport complex, one of which killed a Ugandan soldier of the UN Guard Unit. It was the first lethal indirect-fire attack on AAIA in the 2024–25 series and marked a shift from ground assaults to stand-off IDF against the airport and Halane.

An attacker in military uniform opened fire on a group of Emirati and Bahraini trainers at the General Gordon base, killing four UAE soldiers and a Bahraini officer. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack. The incident highlighted the insider-threat risk at training sites and led to a review of vetting for foreign-supported units.

A suicide bomber blew himself up at the gate of the SYL Hotel, adjacent to the presidential palace, and five or six gunmen stormed inside. The siege ran for about 13 hours; three guards, two security officers and three soldiers were killed along with all the attackers, and 27 people were injured. The hotel had been attacked twice before, and the operation showed that even the palace perimeter zone could be penetrated by a small assault team.

Al-Shabaab detainees in Mogadishu Central Prison seized weapons, threw grenades and attempted a mass breakout. Custodial Corps and army reinforcements contained the attempt after a gunfight that left five prisoners and three soldiers dead and 21 injured. The government said no one escaped; Al-Shabaab claimed hundreds freed. The incident pointed to weapons and communications reaching detainees inside the capital's main prison.

A suicide car bomb exploded outside a café near the Daljirka Daahsoon monument where crowds had gathered to watch the Euro 2024 final. Reports of the toll range from five to more than nine killed, with about 20 injured. The attack, a day after the prison breakout attempt, targeted a predictable civilian gathering and showed the group's attention to timing against televised events.

On a Friday evening a suicide bomber detonated at the Beach View hotel and gunmen then opened fire on beach-goers and diners along Lido Beach. Thirty-seven civilians and a soldier were killed before the six attackers were shot — the deadliest attack in the capital in 2024 and the third major assault on the Lido strip since 2020. Lido's open beachfront and crowd density make it the hardest soft target in the city to protect.

An IED concealed inside a crowded tea shop in Daynile detonated mid-afternoon, killing at least 20 people, several of them security personnel who frequented the venue. The attack came two weeks after Lido Beach and showed Al-Shabaab's reach into the north-western districts along the Afgooye corridor — the same Daynile checkpoints that produce the bulk of Mogadishu's grenade and IED events in 2026.

A suicide car bomber attacked a NISA checkpoint on the Afgooye highway, the main western entry to the city, killing ten people including seven intelligence officers. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. The Afgooye corridor is the primary route by which VBIEDs are assembled in Lower Shabelle and moved toward the capital, and checkpoints on it are repeatedly targeted.

Six mortar rounds landed across the airport and the Halane compound, injuring several people and damaging residences used by ATMIS personnel and diplomats. No group claimed it. It was the second barrage of 2024 and showed the attackers' ability to range both the airfield and the diplomatic enclave from firing points in the city's southern districts.

Mortar rounds struck inside Halane, killing three people and injuring several; ATMIS condemned it as a 'deadly mortar attack'. This was the most lethal of the 2024 barrages and prompted additional counter-IDF measures around the compound's southern and western approaches.

AAIA.loc: Ceelgaabta, presidential motorcade route to airport
AAIA.s: A roadside bomb detonated beside the presidential motorcade at Ceelgaabta as it travelled from Villa Somalia toward the airport. The president was unhurt but reports put the dead at between four and a dozen, including a journalist. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack, which coincided with its spring offensive in Middle and Lower Shabelle and the loss of several towns to the group. It was the closest Al-Shabaab has come to the head of state in the period.

A day after the motorcade bombing, mortar rounds hit the area of the airport where UN personnel board aircraft and landed inside Halane near the Movcon area, just as Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed was arriving. Airport sirens sounded and flights were held; no casualties were reported. The timing against a VIP arrival is the clearest example of Al-Shabaab using IDF for political signalling rather than casualties.

AAIA.loc: AAIA open area, Halane, Kaawo Godey
AAIA.s: Around 06:05 six mortar rounds fell on open ground inside the airport, on Halane and on the Kaawo Godey residential area outside the fence, injuring a woman and a young man. A Turkish Airlines flight diverted to Djibouti and EgyptAir cancelled its service for the day. AUSSOM reported no casualties among its troops. The barrage followed a mortar attack on Warta Nabada and Boondheere the previous day, part of a sustained spring IDF campaign.

At least five mortar shells landed inside the Halane perimeter early on a Monday morning; it was not immediately clear whether anyone was hurt or which installations were hit. It was the third strike on the compound in roughly six weeks and reinforced the assessment that Al-Shabaab could fire on Halane at will from the southern districts.

A bomber dressed in military uniform joined a queue of young recruits at the Damaanyo base gate and detonated a vest at about 09:20, killing 15 recruits and five civilians and injuring 15. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack with inflated casualty figures. The event showed the continued ability to place a person-borne device at a predictable, crowded military access point in Hodan, roughly 3.5 km from AAIA.

At least six mortar rounds hit Halane and properties near the airport two days after the Damaanyo bombing; emergency sirens sounded along the airport perimeter and Al-Shabaab claimed the attack within hours. Somali Guardian counted it as the fourth attack on the base in recent weeks. Damage was limited to property, but the cadence (four barrages in nine weeks) is the densest IDF campaign against AAIA/Halane in the period.

A suicide bomber reached the morning roll-call at the Jaalle Siyaad academy, headquarters of the 14th October Brigade, and detonated among officers; gunfire followed. Four SNA officers were killed and several injured. Six senior officers were detained over the security breach and the ministry restricted reporting. Coming two years after a deadlier 2023 bombing at the same academy, it underlined persistent insider and access-control weaknesses at Hodan military sites.

AAIA.loc: Godka Jilow prison, near Villa Somalia
AAIA.t: VBIED + armed assault in NISA-style vehicles/uniforms
AAIA.s: A car bomb breached the entrance of the Godka Jilow underground prison near the presidential palace and a seven-man team in military-style uniforms, driving vehicles painted to resemble NISA's, attempted to free detained fighters. The siege lasted about six hours before all seven attackers were killed; the government said no prisoners escaped and did not publish its own losses. The attack came hours after the city reopened dozens of roads and is the most recent confirmed complex assault by Al-Shabaab in the capital.

AAIA.t: Political violence: government shelling/assault on opposition compounds
AAIA.tg: Residences of ex-PM Khaire and ex-President Sharif
AAIA.s: Over two days government forces shelled and assaulted the Barmuudo compound of former PM Hassan Ali Khaire and then the Marinayo residence of former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, after the collapse of election talks and the expiry of the presidential mandate. NISA chief Mahad Salad negotiated Khaire's withdrawal and escorted him back to his residence inside the AAIA perimeter, where opposition leaders had been based before dispersing to clan areas. Western ambassadors, speaking from Halane, pressed for a halt. Casualty figures were never verified. Not an Al-Shabaab event, but the clearest case of Mogadishu's political conflict reaching the airport perimeter.

Defence Minister Ahmed Moalim Fiqi said authorities had removed 260 armed men from opposition leaders' residences in Mogadishu, alleging the UAE had armed the opposition and that Puntland- and Jubaland-linked forces had been brought into the city. He denied any plan to arrest opposition leaders. Only the government's account is available. The operation is the precursor indicator for a repeat of the June clashes.

AAIA.loc: Hormuud HQ, Bakara Market & airport road
AAIA.s: Police entered Hormuud's headquarters in Bakara Market and its main management office on the road to the airport under a court warrant, reportedly in connection with the Southwest State fighting. No violence was reported. The relevance for AAIA is the use of the airport road for a politically charged security operation and the risk of escalation involving Somalia's largest private company.
