BRIEF.CZ: No terrorism, sabotage, violent unrest or major transport disruption was confirmed in Czechia between 9 and 23 October; the only notable event was the 17 October Senate runoff in which the opposition won and Babiš's ANO took no seats, with no incidents reported. Czechia remains inside the regional Russian sabotage pattern that Germany's armed forces rated a significant threat on 21 October and that produced a spy arrest in Brandenburg on 22 October, but nothing in the window points to an active plot on Czech soil. Business travel to Prague and regional centres is routine.
BRIEF.GB: The UK picture through 23 October is dominated by state threats rather than street disorder: the RAF Fairford investigation moved on 20 October to National Security Act re-arrests for assisting Iranian intelligence, MI5 said on 13 October that Iran and Russia are both expanding hybrid campaigns and that Iran-linked operations produced more than 50 arrests in a year, and the Home Secretary set out new sanctions and powers on 12 October. The national terrorism threat level remains Severe. No attack occurred in the window and daily business travel is unaffected, but US-linked military sites, Jewish community venues and Iranian-dissident targets carry elevated risk; the cost-of-living unrest in France, Italy and Belgium has not spread to Britain.
BRIEF.DE: Germany's state-threat environment hardened further this week: federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian national in Brandenburg on 22 October for gathering military intelligence for Russia, including on NATO eastern-flank sites and defence-industry production, one day after the Bundeswehr rated the Russian sabotage threat to its own forces as significant for the first time, citing the explosive-laden drone found near Wunstorf air base. A perimeter breach at Leipzig/Halle airport on 17-18 October closed the north runway and triggered a major police search before two learner drivers admitted crashing through the fence. For travellers the practical impact remains sporadic airport disruption and heightened security around military, Jewish and Israeli sites; the violent unrest in France and Italy has not spread to Germany.
BRIEF.SK: No terrorism, sabotage, violent protest or transport disruption was confirmed in Slovakia between 9 and 23 October. The risk remains political: the Fico government will hold the first Slovak-Russian intergovernmental commission since 2022 in Moscow on 26 October, focused on gas, oil and nuclear energy, and has restored military attachés with Russia for the first time in four years, deepening divergence from EU and NATO allies and feeding peaceful opposition demonstrations. Business travel to Bratislava and Košice is routine.
BRIEF.AT: Austria recorded no significant security incident between 9 and 23 October; the only notable event remains the Vienna counter-espionage case, in which two Ukrainians arrested on 5 October are held on suspicion of working for a foreign intelligence service, while two Ukrainska Pravda journalists detained on 8 October were released without charge and prosecutors said on 12 October the arrests were unrelated to their profession. Vienna remains a hub for intelligence activity linked to the war in Ukraine, but the threat to travellers is low and the cost-of-living unrest in France, Italy and Belgium has not reached Austria.
BRIEF.BE: Belgium remains the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: union strike days on 9 and 12 October disrupted Brussels Airport, rail, public transport and schools, and student-led protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, with police using tear gas and water cannon. The federal budget talks failed again on 21 October and Prime Minister De Wever told parliament on 22 October that an agreement is now expected next week, so the trigger for further union action stays live; the socialist FGTB holds a mandate for a general strike in late November if its red lines are crossed. Expect Friday and weekend disruption in central Brussels and plan airport transfers with margin while the budget is unresolved.
BRIEF.IT: Italy's two crises moved in opposite directions on 22 October: trucker roadblocks over diesel prices that had emptied supermarket shelves and fuel pumps across the south, halted buffalo mozzarella production and disrupted ambulance and hospital access in Naples began to lift in Sicily and Calabria as the cabinet approved an aid decree for hauliers, farmers and fishers, while Meloni warned that remaining blockades and tyre-slashing of other drivers would be treated as intimidation. In the north, the 17-18 October riots in Milan, Turin, Bologna, Brescia and Bergamo led to 500 extra soldiers for Milan and a new violent-protest offence, and the self-styled 17 October movement has called rallies for Saturday 24 October in Milan, Florence, Bologna, Turin, Rome, Naples and other cities. Plan movements away from city centres on 24 October and keep fuel, routing and regional-airport contingencies for southern Italy until roadblocks are fully cleared.
BRIEF.ES: Spain's immediate risk remains environmental: Storm Adam killed four people in the Valencia region and Catalonia on 17-19 October, with 632 mm of rain in 36 hours at Pego, more than 2,000 evacuated and up to 800,000 people briefly under shelter-in-place orders; red alerts have been lifted but clean-up in Oliva, Pego, Els Poblets and the Marina Alta continues to disrupt secondary roads and commuter rail. The 18 October Basque terrorism arrests, involving data on security forces and a suspected arms and explosives cache, are the first such case in years and appear contained. Social tension is elevated ahead of the 29 November early election, with a 24-hour Renfe train drivers' strike called for 29 October and unions calling a general strike for 11 November, but protests have stayed largely peaceful; terrorism and crime indicators are otherwise unchanged.
BRIEF.FR: France remains the epicentre of the European unrest wave: the 17 October riots torched Limoges town hall, damaged or looted more than 3,000 shops and put some 2,500 people in custody, and the government has responded with targeted night curfews in Paris, Lyon, Lille, Nice, Bordeaux and Marseille, protest bans in Paris, Lyon, Lille and Grenoble and troops alongside police for the Saturday 24 October protest day, which yellow-vest activists and the CGT union have joined. On 22 October a Paris administrative court overturned the police ban and thousands rallied peacefully under heavy policing, while Macron said the general rule for the coming days is no demonstrations and prefects will impose alternative routes; the Paris curfew around République and Les Halles runs until 26 October. Risk stays high for at least two to three weeks; avoid central Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Lille and Montpellier on 24 October and plan movements around curfew and protest-ban perimeters.
BRIEF.PL: Poland's window was front-loaded: three school stabbings in four days that killed a custodian and triggered checks of nearly 50,000 schools, German arrests on 12 October of two Turkish nationals suspected of the Russian-directed Starlink station arson near Warsaw, and the 19 October detention in Łódź of a Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course on spying suspicion. The last week has been quieter, but Tusk warned on 17 October of larger-scale Russian sabotage and provocations before Christmas, with railways and border crossings supplying Ukraine most exposed, and Germany's 21 October threat upgrade and 22 October spy arrest reinforce the regional pattern. Warsaw remains fully workable.
BRIEF.NO: Norway remains a low-risk operating environment; the only in-window events affecting movement were the heavily policed 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Støre and Stubb and Zelensky's 21 October visit to the Storting, both of which passed without incident. The one domestic security operation was Økokrim's 14 October arrest of five people in the Bergen area over fraud and bribery on NATO ship-supply contracts, a white-collar case with no bearing on travellers. No violence, sabotage or transport disruption affecting travellers occurred between 9 and 23 October; friction with Russia over the Arctic, sanctions and coastal espionage continues without change to travel advice.
BRIEF.FI: Finland is safe for travel and operations, but the south-eastern coast between Loviisa and the Russian border is subject to short-notice air and sea closures whenever Ukraine mounts large strikes on St Petersburg; the Defence Forces imposed such restrictions on three consecutive mornings on 16, 17 and 18 October, the last lasting from 02:45 to 09:43 during the record attack on St Petersburg, with no drones crossing into Finland. No violence occurred on Finnish territory between 9 and 23 October. The eastern land border remains closed to civilian traffic, GNSS interference persists in the Gulf of Finland, and the government is building counter-drone capacity, most recently with 32 million euros in EU funding for the Border Guard confirmed on 15 October.
BRIEF.EE: No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 9 and 23 October 2026; the most recent notable event remains the August arson attack on Milrem Robotics in Tallinn, which Tallinn attributed to Russian special services on 29 September. In-window reporting is dominated by deterrence, resilience and domestic politics: Foreign Minister Tsahkna's 15 October warning that Russia will intensify hybrid attacks on critical infrastructure and defence firms, nearly 32 million euros in EU funding confirmed on 16 October for eastern-border drone surveillance, and the minority government's survival of an opposition no-confidence motion on 19 October. Travel to Tallinn is routine; vehicle traffic through the Narva crossing remains suspended and any onward travel into Russia carries serious detention risk.
BRIEF.RU: Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: Reuters reported the 18 October assault on St Petersburg and the Leningrad region killed one and injured 15, set the St Petersburg oil terminal and an oil depot ablaze and hit Ozon and VK logistics and data centres as Russia claimed 1,015 drones downed in one night, while on 22 October 630 drones were sent towards Moscow, wounding two, and drones struck apartment buildings and a clinic in Lipetsk, hours after a drone killed a 19-year-old in Bryansk region on 21 October. Air travel is unreliable, and Western nationals face arbitrary detention on espionage or sabotage pretexts, with the FSB announcing the arrest of a Swedish national on 15 October and a Japanese journalist on 13 October; the 21 October release of American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff's St Petersburg talks with Putin, who agreed to resume US-mediated trilateral talks as early as November, shows detainees are treated as diplomatic currency. Western companies should treat Russia as no-go for travel; remaining staff need independent exit plans via Finland or the Baltics, noting Finland's land border is closed to civilian crossing.
BRIEF.TR: No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye in the 9-23 October window; the operational picture is dominated by the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight dead per AFP on 19 October) and by the political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October (Reuters), continuing detentions of opposition-run municipal officials, and Reuters-reported detention orders for 31 suspects in the investment-fund probe on 21 October. Press organisations have called nationwide demonstrations for 24 October, and the Imamoglu trial calendar and November's COP31 in Antalya raise the likelihood of protests and heavy policing in Istanbul and Ankara.
BRIEF.IQ: The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: a missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October (Reuters), the latest in a series of Iranian strikes on exile camps on 8, 12 and 17 October, and on 20 October Tehran's ambassador said Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups, a step Iraqi security officials had told AFP they refused. Outside the region, a roadside bomb killed an army brigadier and a soldier south of Kirkuk on 14 October in the second Islamic State-linked attack there this month, a blast at a PMF headquarters in Baghdad killed one member and wounded four on 17 October (Reuters), and Iraq closed the Sheeb crossing with Iran on 21 October for a security review. Erbil and Sulaimaniyah commercial flights continue, but with coalition air defences gone since the 30 September US withdrawal the trajectory in Erbil province is toward more frequent unanswered strikes.
BRIEF.MA: Morocco recorded no kinetic security incident between 9 and 23 October that a wire service confirmed; the environment remains political. The new four-party government under Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri was sworn in on 16 October and presented a programme to parliament on 19 October targeting 5% average growth in 2027-2031 (Reuters), while Spain's handling of the Ceuta migrant backlog drew a rights complaint from eight charities (Reuters, 19 October) and Algeria's 11 October announcement of 61 Moroccans arrested in Oran keeps the Algiers-Rabat confrontation sharp ahead of the 31 October MINURSO renewal vote. The last notable kinetic incident remains the Polisario rocket attack near Smara on 5 May 2026 (one civilian injured, older).
BRIEF.DZ: No terrorist attack, clash or significant protest was wire-confirmed in Algeria for 9-23 October; the environment is stable but heavily securitised and the state continues to frame domestic problems as foreign-backed subversion. The one confirmed development is the DGSN's 11 October announcement that 61 Moroccan nationals were arrested in Oran on suspicion of preparing sabotage (Le Monde/AFP), which raises the temperature with Rabat ahead of the 31 October MINURSO vote; Spain's postponement of the Madrid high-level summit that had been planned for 20-21 October and the September rupture with the UAE underline a more combative foreign posture. The jihadist threat is low but not zero (failed suicide attack near a Blida police station in April and army-militant clashes in Tebessa in March, both older); the Sahel border belt and the far south remain off-limits for routine corporate travel.
BRIEF.TN: Tunisia's risk profile is rising: on 22 October police fired tear gas at protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of Tunis, after the death of a man in custody, with parallel clashes in Jebeniana and Agareb in Sfax governorate and student protests in Sfax city (Reuters), five days after the UGTT-led march of 17 October, the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years. On 21 October a military court sentenced opposition leader Olfa Hamdi, a US citizen, to four years in prison for plotting against state security (Reuters), the latest in a series of prosecutions of critics. Reuters reported fears of a wider wave of violent protest over living conditions and public services; expect further protest calls, possible strike action and localised unrest in working-class suburbs and the interior, while the Chaambi and Libyan-frontier zones remain restricted.
BRIEF.EG: No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was wire-confirmed in Egypt for 9-23 October, but the external-security profile is rising. Parliament will hold a roll-call vote on 26 October on President Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis; on 21-22 October the foreign minister and intelligence chief carried a letter from Sisi to the Saudi crown prince stating that support would be limited to defending Saudi territory, and Cairo urged exploring 'every opportunity' for a political settlement (Reuters). The Houthi-run parliament has warned Cairo that intervention would threaten its internal stability, so a deployment would expose Egyptian and Suez-linked targets to retaliation. On the southern frontier, the 10 October air strikes on the Jabal al-Uqaydat gold-mining site killed at least 72 miners according to Sudan's Emergency Lawyers (France 24/AFP); North Sinai remains a restricted military zone and the Sudan border belt should be treated as no-go, while Cairo, Alexandria, the Canal cities and Red Sea resorts remain workable with standard precautions.
BRIEF.LY: Libya remains Critical and the trend is rising: on 22 October individuals entered the AGOCO crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and shut the valve on the Hamada-Tahara pipeline, cutting output at both fields (Reuters), the second forced pipeline closure in western Libya in five weeks; on 21 October armed men stormed the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose a disputed deputy head, drawing UNSMIL's strongest condemnation and a warning of targeted sanctions; and on 18 October an 82mm mortar blast killed at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency personnel during training in Zawiya (Reuters). Human Rights Watch said on 14 October that eastern authorities had executed at least 31 people since late August after military trials. The political track is comparatively convergent: SRSG Tetteh told the Security Council on 14 October the process had made 'encouraging progress' while urging it to 'hold spoilers accountable', and the east-based parliament's 20 October approval of the 2019 Türkiye maritime deal (Reuters) lowers the risk of a renewed national split while drawing rejections from Greece, Egypt, Israel and the EU; UNSMIL's mandate expires 31 October and renewal is expected. The August drone strikes on the Zawiya refinery, the September Sharara-Zawiya pipeline shutdown and the 10 August car-bomb killing of the LNA intelligence chief in Benghazi remain the baseline of targeted violence and infrastructure disruption.
BRIEF.NG: The north-east is in its most dangerous phase in years: Boko Haram overran the army base at Guzamala on the night of 13 October, killing at least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard (Reuters, 15 Oct), and a mine-and-ambush attack on a patrol between Gamboru Ngala and the Cameroon border on 17 October killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF members (Reuters, 19 Oct); in the north-west, bandits killed at least 20 in a military-escorted traders' convoy in Bukkuyum, Zamfara, on 10 October (Reuters, 12 Oct), so armed escort cannot be treated as sufficient mitigation on rural roads. The imported Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja, confirmed on 20 October, was not tested until 13 days after the patient fell ill; 44 contacts, mostly healthcare workers, are being traced and the health minister said on 22 October there is no evidence of community spread, but travellers should expect airport screening, avoid non-essential use of private clinics in the FCT and confirm medical-evacuation cover. Lagos and the south recorded no wire-confirmed major security incident in the window; rating held at 3 with a rising trend.
BRIEF.NE: The deadliest incident of the window struck the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen in three vehicles ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP), on the only corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic between Agadez and the uranium belt, and the military escort aboard did not prevent it. The release on 21 October of Austrian Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, both kidnapped in Agadez in 2025 (BBC, 22 Oct), closes two long-running hostage cases but confirms that foreigners in the Agadez region are kidnap targets. The civil picture is deteriorating in parallel: the petrol shortage reached Niamey on 18 October with a fuel-export ban in force since 12 October (AFP), ground movement is increasingly unreliable, and frontline frustration after the late-September ISSP assaults in Tillaberi, Africa Corps dependence and the junta's purge of critics since the failed 29 August mutiny keep coup and reprisal risk elevated; rating held at 4.
BRIEF.ML: Mali is in open, multi-front war: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a fuel blockade since late April, while Islamic State Sahel Province's killing of at least 48 civilians (provisional local tolls up to 70+) across at least five localities in Menaka on 18-19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, shows the IS affiliate escalating in the east even as it fights JNIM across the Burkina border; the army said on 19 October it had struck a major ISSP base 65 km south-west of Menaka (AP). The army's re-entry into Kidal on 6 October after the separatists' withdrawal is a morale win but the supply picture is unchanged, with fuel reaching Bamako only in escorted convoys. Human Rights Watch's 19 October report (Reuters) documents indiscriminate Malian and Africa Corps drone strikes on a market and a health centre and the execution of 19 captured soldiers by JNIM and FLA fighters, sharpening reprisal risk against anyone associated with the state or its partners; rating held at 4, all travel should be deferred.
BRIEF.SD: The war is in a drone-dominated phase in which both sides strike far behind the front lines: AFP counted at least 80 dead when army drones hit a transport hub beside Al-Dibab market in West Kordofan on 18 October, AP and AFP reported a strike on central Nyala on 19 October that killed 17 and an RSF drone attack the same morning on a house east of Khartoum airport that killed four, and the army's 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market across the South Sudan border killed at least 153 by the Abyei administration's count. The UN condemned the wave of strikes on 19 and 20 October, a Geneva consultative meeting on 21 October produced no ceasefire track, and the AU Commission condemned the attacks on 22 October; army-held Khartoum, Port Sudan and the eastern dams remain inside RSF drone range while Kordofan and Darfur are active ground fronts. Rating 4 retained, trend rising on the scale of civilian-targeted strikes; there is no basis for any corporate travel.
BRIEF.SS: South Sudan is absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October strike on Amiet market in Abyei, which hit a fuel depot and which a Sudanese military officer told AP targeted RSF-bound fuel tankers, killed at least 153 by the Abyei administration's count given to Reuters and AP and displaced about 8,000; UNISFA said on 21 October that many remain missing and the toll is expected to rise. Juba summoned Sudan's ambassador and the UN Secretary-General demanded accountability on 20 October, but Juba has no means to deter further strikes on supply corridors through its territory. Internally, the 9 October Rumbek fighting (71 dead by the government's preliminary count) shows how quickly intercommunal violence can engulf a state capital, and the political transition remains brittle with Machar on trial and a 22 December election timetable few observers expect to hold. Juba itself is calmer; expect further flashpoints in Abyei, Lakes, Jonglei and Upper Nile as the dry season opens roads to armed movement.
BRIEF.SO: As of 23 October, AFP-confirmed reporting shows Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces holding Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle (30 km from Baidoa), leaving Baidoa as the only major Bay town under the federally backed South West administration, which has vowed to retake the districts while Ethiopian AUSSOM troops stayed inside their bases; a fight for Baidoa remains the base case and the Mogadishu–Baidoa road through Buurhakaba is cut. The electoral commission's 15 October timetable (parliament 15 April, president 15 May 2027) is rejected by the opposition, Puntland and Jubaland, sustaining the risk of armed political confrontation in Mogadishu, and IOM now projects up to 874,000 flood displacements by December with the Shabelle rising at Jowhar and the Juba at Dollow, which will degrade road movement in Hiraan, Middle Shabelle and Gedo. No large or complex al-Shabaab attack in the capital or at Aden Adde airport was wire-reported between 9 and 23 October; rating 4 and rising trend are retained and posture remains no-go outside the airport/Halane enclave, with Bay and Bakool regions and the Mogadishu–Baidoa road closed.
BRIEF.ET: Tigray is easing but not settled: federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa, Axum and Zalambessa, Al Jazeera reported shops and banks reopening in Mekelle on 22 October, and Abiy's six-month caretaker administration named on 16 October is preparing an election, yet the TPLF rejects it, the Ethiopia-Eritrea confrontation remains frozen with troops facing each other at Zalambessa and Rubio warned on 17 October that troop surges on both sides of the border could turn into a broader conflict. A new southern flashpoint opened on 21-22 October when fighting between Oromia and Somali regional forces in Moyale sent hundreds of Ethiopians across the border into Kenya with gunfire continuing on 22 October, so the trend is changed from easing to flat: Tigray calmer, but the Amhara Fano insurgency, the Oromia-Somali border and the Eritrean front all remain live. Rating 4 retained for the country as a whole; roads north of Addis remain unsafe and Addis Ababa functions under a heavy security posture.
BRIEF.ER: Eritrea remains a party to the Tigray confrontation in all but name: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, Asmara asked the Council for Chapter VII deterrent measures against Ethiopia on 10 October, and Ethiopian troops reached Zalambessa on the border on 13 October. Asmara's 21 October foreign ministry statement restated a purely defensive posture and denied any invasion or irredentist claim, and its UN ambassador told US diplomats there is no crisis, but diplomatic ties remain severed, Rubio said on 17 October that troops are surging on both sides of the border and that this could turn into a broader conflict, and Abiy continues to assert Ethiopia's need for sea access. A cross-border escalation within weeks remains plausible; internal reporting from Eritrea is almost nil, so assume mobilisation, communications restrictions and no exit options if the border war widens. Rating 3 retained.
BRIEF.DJ: No violent security incident was recorded inside Djibouti in the past 14 days; the major event remains the 8-9 October migrant shipwreck off Obock (139 dead and 84 missing per IOM), while UNHCR counted 3,836 refugees arrived from Yemen in Obock region by 17 October with an acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in the Markazi camp. The exposure is external: Houthi forces fighting for Yemen's Red Sea coast keep the Bab el-Mandeb, Camp Lemonnier and the port within missile and drone range, and Djibouti and China jointly flagged a deteriorating Red Sea security situation on 22 October as the US ordered some diplomats out of Saudi Arabia; the Ethiopia-Djibouti corridor runs through Afar, where fighting has decreased but not ended. Djibouti City and the ports operate normally; rating 2 retained, monitor corridor security in Afar, war-risk premiums and any Houthi targeting of shipping or foreign bases.
BRIEF.KE: Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating normally but the risk picture carries a health overlay: the imported Bundibugyo Ebola case has produced a nine-case cluster of relatives and healthcare workers as of 20 October, all detected in quarantine with 134 of 135 contacts traced and no transmission outside the group, and the US moved Kenya to Level 3 on 19 October while keeping Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu and Tana River at Do Not Travel over kidnapping and terrorism. A new northern flashpoint opened on 21-22 October when fighting between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional forces in Moyale sent hundreds of Ethiopians across the border and stray rounds wounded a woman and struck a police officer on the Kenyan side. The al-Shabaab IED threat to security convoys persists along the Somali border, the 14 October fuel price rise adds a cost-of-living trigger and the 2027 election cycle is under way, so assume rapid escalation potential around any further price or tax measure. Rating 3 retained.
BRIEF.CD: Rating held at 4. Former president Joseph Kabila's launch of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) in Goma on 12 October, absorbing AFC/M23 with Nangaa, Bisimwa, Kaniki and Makenga as his deputies and a declared aim of ending 'tyranny' by force (Reuters), has been met by Kinshasa with a nationwide ban on 13 parties including Kabila's PPRD on 15 October and government spokesman Muyaya's statement that Kabila has formalised an 'attack against the Republic' (DW, 17 Oct); the African Union on 20 October warned against any seizure of power by force and called for respect of the ceasefire (DW), and Belgium's foreign minister condemned the FRN as 'unacceptable' on 21 October, while the Belgian money-laundering raids on Tshisekedi relatives (Reuters, 15 Oct) and the presidency's ban on contact with the Belgian embassy keep Kinshasa's relationship with its main European partner strained. Fighting between FRN/M23 and FARDC-Wazalendo continues with drones and artillery in South Kivu (Walungu/Kaziba, Minembwe) and Masisi, and UN OCHA confirmed attacks around the Rhoe displacement site (12 Oct) and near Pimbo on National Road 27 (13 Oct) in Ituri that disrupted the Ebola response. The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak reached an eighth province, North Ubangi, on 18 October (Reuters) and stood at 9,704 confirmed cases and 4,687 deaths in DRC on 21 October with nine cases in Kenya and one in Nigeria (US CDC); Goma, Bukavu, Uvira and all of North/South Kivu and Ituri remain no-go, and Kinshasa is operable with advance planning but carries elevated risk of politically driven unrest, arbitrary detention of persons linked to banned parties and sudden movement restrictions.
BRIEF.BR: Brazil votes on Sunday 25 October in a presidential runoff that Quaest (Reuters, 21 Oct) puts at 45-44 for Flávio Bolsonaro over Lula, within the margin of error, and on 20-21 October each camp filed a petition at the Superior Electoral Court to disqualify the other (AFP, 22 Oct), so a narrow result is likely to be contested in court and on the street. Rio remains the operational concern: Queimados' economic development secretary was shot dead by Military Police during a stop on Avenida Brasil on 19 October and five officers were suspended (Agência Brasil, 20 Oct), while the state electoral court's 15 October troop request for 15 metro municipalities stands. Rating held at 2: the only wire-confirmed violent incidents in the window were a police shooting in Rio and a resolved school hostage-taking in Curitiba (AP, 9 Oct), neither involving foreigners; trend set to rising for the runoff weekend only.
BRIEF.CO: President de la Espriella's government is escalating: a 22 October air strike on an ELN camp in El Tambo, Cauca killed nine guerrillas including the Southwestern War Front's military chief alias Marcos Pacífico (DW, 23 Oct), the fifth bombing of his term, three days after he ordered a 'total offensive' against the ELN and FARC dissidents from Arauca and demanded the ELN free five hostages including two CTI investigators (Presidencia, 19 Oct). Armed groups are answering on the Cauca stretch of the Pan-American Highway, where a 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza injured three civilians and clashes on 9-10 October killed two soldiers (AP, 12 Oct). Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena recorded no wire-confirmed attack in the window; rating held at 3 with the trend rising because retaliation against infrastructure and security forces in the south-west and on the Venezuelan border is the pattern after each strike.
BRIEF.VE: The first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years passed on 22 October without wire-reported violence: thousands marched in Caracas, Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal and Maracaibo for a 2027 election date, Machado's return and the release of more than 320 political prisoners, with a thin security-force presence even as the ruling party held a rival march from the same square (Reuters, 22 Oct). The US-backed talks between the interim government and the Figuera opposition faction closed their third round on 21 October, and Washington lifted sanctions on National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez on 14 October as that round opened (Reuters, 14 Oct). No US military action, deadly unrest or detention of a foreign national was wire-confirmed in the window; rating held at 3 because the transition remains unscheduled and the street is now an active lever.
